sentences.zh: 段秀實段秀實，字成公，隴州汧陽人也。

translations.literal: Duan Xiushi, Duan Xiushi, courtesy name Chenggong, was a native of Qianyang in Long prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Xiushi, whose courtesy name was Chenggong, came from Qianyang in Long prefecture.

sentences.zh: 祖達，左衛中郎。

translations.literal: His grandfather Da was a middle officer of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Da served as a middle officer of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 父行琛，洮州司馬，以秀實贈揚州大都督。

translations.literal: His father Xingchen was secretary of Tao prefecture; because of Xiushi he was posthumously made Great Governor-General of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xingchen had been secretary of Tao prefecture; on account of Xiushi's achievements he was posthumously enfeoffed as Great Governor-General of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 秀實性至孝，六歲，母疾，水漿不入口七日，疾有間，然後飲食。

translations.literal: Xiushi was by nature extremely filial; at age six, when his mother fell ill, he took no food or drink for seven days, and only after her illness abated did he eat and drink again.
translations.idiomatic: Xiushi was profoundly filial. When he was six, his mother fell ill and he refused all food and drink for seven days; he resumed eating only after she had begun to recover.

sentences.zh: 及長，沈厚有斷。

translations.literal: When he grew up, he was deep and steady and decisive.
translations.idiomatic: As an adult he was grave, steadfast, and resolute.

sentences.zh: 天寶四載，安西節度馬靈察署為別將，從討護蜜有功，授安西府別將。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianbao, Anxi military commissioner Ma Lingcha appointed him deputy general; he followed in the campaign against Humi with merit and was made deputy general of the Anxi command.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao year 4, Anxi commissioner Ma Lingcha appointed him deputy general. He took part in the attack on Humi with distinction and was given the post of deputy general of the Anxi command.

sentences.zh: 七載，高仙芝代靈察，舉兵圍怛邏斯，黑衣救至，仙芝大衄，軍士相失。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Gao Xianzhi replaced Lingcha, raised troops and besieged Talas; the Black Robes came to the rescue, Xianzhi suffered a great defeat, and soldiers lost one another.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7, Gao Xianzhi succeeded Lingcha and led an army to besiege Talas. When the Black Robe forces arrived to relieve the city, Xianzhi was routed and the troops scattered.

sentences.zh: 夜中聞都將李嗣業之聲，因大呼責之曰：「軍敗而求免，非丈夫也。

translations.literal: In the night he heard the voice of chief commander Li Siye and thereupon shouted to rebuke him, saying: 'The army is defeated yet you seek to escape—this is not the conduct of a true man.'
translations.idiomatic: During the night he heard chief commander Li Siye and shouted a rebuke: "The army has been beaten and you seek only to save yourself—that is not how a true man behaves."

sentences.zh: 」嗣業甚慚，遂與秀實收合散卒，復得成軍。

translations.literal: ' Siye was deeply ashamed, and thereupon together with Xiushi gathered the scattered troops and again formed an army.
translations.idiomatic: " Siye was deeply ashamed. He and Xiushi then rallied the scattered soldiers and restored the force.

sentences.zh: 師還，嗣業請於仙芝，以秀實為判官，授斥候府果毅。

translations.literal: When the army returned, Siye requested of Xianzhi that Xiushi be made staff judge, and he was appointed fruit commander of the reconnaissance command.
translations.idiomatic: After the army returned, Siye asked Xianzhi to appoint Xiushi as his staff judge and had him made fruit commander of the reconnaissance command.

sentences.zh: 十二載，封常清代仙芝，討大勃律，師次賀薩勞城，戰而勝。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, Feng Changqing replaced Xianzhi and campaigned against Greater Bolü; the army halted at Hesalao city, fought, and won.
translations.idiomatic: In year 12, Feng Changqing succeeded Xianzhi and marched against Greater Bolü. The army encamped at Hesalao city, gave battle, and prevailed.

sentences.zh: 常清逐之，秀實進曰：「賊兵羸，餌我也，請備左右，搜其山林。

translations.literal: Changqing pursued them; Xiushi advanced and said: 'The enemy troops are weak—they are baiting us. Please guard both flanks and search the mountain forests.'
translations.idiomatic: As Changqing pressed the pursuit, Xiushi urged him forward: "The enemy is feigning weakness to lure us on. Post guards on both flanks and search the wooded hills."

sentences.zh: 」遂殲其伏，改綏德府折衝。

translations.literal: ' Thereupon they annihilated the ambush force, and he was transferred to be strike commander of Suide prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: " They destroyed the ambush and he was transferred to strike commander of Suide prefecture.

sentences.zh: 肅宗即位於靈武，征安西兵節度使梁宰，宰潛懷異圖。

translations.literal: Suzong took the throne at Lingwu and summoned Anxi troops; military commissioner Liang Zai secretly harbored a different design.
translations.idiomatic: When Suzong acceded at Lingwu he called up the Anxi army, but commissioner Liang Zai was secretly plotting treason.

sentences.zh: 秀實謂嗣業曰：「豈有天子告急，臣下晏然，信浮妄之說，豈明公之意耶？

translations.literal: Xiushi said to Siye: 'How can there be the Son of Heaven reporting urgency while his subjects remain at ease, believing empty and false talk—is this your lordship's intent?'
translations.idiomatic: Xiushi said to Siye, "Can it be right that the Son of Heaven is in distress while his servants sit idle, trusting idle rumors? Is that what you intend?"

sentences.zh: 」嗣業遂見宰，請發兵，從之。

translations.literal: ' Siye thereupon went to see Zai and requested that troops be sent; Zai followed this.
translations.idiomatic: " Siye then went to Zai and pressed him to mobilize; Zai agreed.

sentences.zh: 乃出步騎五千，令嗣業統赴朔方，以秀實為援，累有戰功。

translations.literal: They then sent out five thousand infantry and cavalry, ordered Siye to command them to Shuo-fang, with Xiushi as support, and repeatedly achieved battle merit.
translations.idiomatic: Five thousand foot and horse were dispatched under Siye's command toward Shuo-fang, with Xiushi as his second; they won repeated victories.

sentences.zh: 而秀實父歿，哀毀過禮。

translations.literal: But Xiushi's father died, and his grief and devastation exceeded the rites.
translations.idiomatic: Xiushi's father then died, and his mourning exceeded what the rites prescribed.

sentences.zh: 嗣業既授節制，思秀實如失左右手，表請起復，為義王友，充節度判官。

translations.literal: After Siye received command authority, he missed Xiushi as if he had lost his right and left hands, memorialized to recall him from mourning, made him companion to the Prince of Yi, and appointed him staff judge of the commission.
translations.idiomatic: Once Siye held independent command he felt as if he had lost both hands without Xiushi, memorialized for his recall from mourning, appointed him companion to the Prince of Yi, and made him staff judge.

sentences.zh: 安慶緒奔鄴，嗣業與諸軍圍之，安西輜重委於河內。

translations.literal: An Qingxu fled to Ye; Siye with the various armies besieged him, and Anxi baggage and heavy stores were left at Henei.
translations.idiomatic: When An Qingxu fled to Ye, Siye joined the allied armies in besieging him, while the Anxi baggage train was deposited at Henei.

sentences.zh: 乃奏秀實為懷州長史，知軍州，加節度留後。

translations.literal: He thereupon memorialized that Xiushi be made chief administrator of Huai prefecture, with charge of the army prefecture, and additionally acting military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to appoint Xiushi chief administrator of Huai prefecture with military and civil authority, and additionally as acting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 諸軍進戰於愁思岡，嗣業為流矢所中，卒於軍，眾推安西兵馬使荔非元禮代之。

translations.literal: The armies advanced to fight at Chousi Hill; Siye was struck by a stray arrow and died in camp; the troops promoted Anxi army commander Lifei Yuanli to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: The allied forces fought at Chousi Hill. Siye was killed by a stray arrow in camp, and the men chose Anxi army commander Lifei Yuanli as his successor.

sentences.zh: 秀實聞嗣業之喪，乃遺先鋒將白孝德書，令發卒護嗣業喪送河內。

translations.literal: Xiushi heard of Siye's death and sent a letter to vanguard general Bai Xiaode, ordering him to dispatch troops to escort Siye's coffin to Henei.
translations.idiomatic: On hearing of Siye's death, Xiushi wrote to vanguard general Bai Xiaode instructing him to send troops to escort the coffin to Henei.

sentences.zh: 秀實率將吏哭待於境，傾私財以奉葬事。

translations.literal: Xiushi led officers and clerks to weep and await at the border, pouring out private wealth to supply the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: Xiushi led his officers to the border to receive the procession in mourning and spent his private fortune on the funeral.

sentences.zh: 元禮多其義，奏試光祿少卿，依前節度判官。

translations.literal: Yuanli admired his righteousness and memorialized him for probationary vice director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, continuing as before as staff judge of the commission.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanli admired his conduct and recommended him for probationary vice director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments while retaining him as staff judge.

sentences.zh: 邙山之敗，軍徙翼城，元禮為麾下所殺，將佐亦多遇害，而秀實獨以智全。

translations.literal: After the defeat at Mang Hill the army moved to Yicheng; Yuanli was killed by his subordinates, and many staff officers were also harmed, but Xiushi alone preserved himself through wisdom.
translations.idiomatic: After the defeat at Mang Hill the army withdrew to Yicheng. Yuanli was murdered by his own men and many officers perished, but Xiushi alone escaped through his wits.

sentences.zh: 眾推白孝德為節度使，人心稍定。

translations.literal: The troops promoted Bai Xiaode as military commissioner, and hearts were somewhat settled.
translations.idiomatic: The troops installed Bai Xiaode as commissioner and morale steadied somewhat.

sentences.zh: 又遷試光祿卿，為孝德判官。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to probationary director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and served as Xiaode's staff judge.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to probationary director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and served as Xiaode's staff judge.

sentences.zh: 孝德改鎮邠寧，奏秀實試太常卿、支度營田二副使。

translations.literal: Xiaode was transferred to command Binning and memorialized Xiushi as probationary director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and as deputy for supply and army farms.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaode was reassigned to Binning, he recommended Xiushi as probationary director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and deputy for supply and army farms.

sentences.zh: 大軍西遷，所過掠奪。

translations.literal: The great army moved west and wherever it passed it plundered.
translations.idiomatic: As the main army marched west it looted every district along the route.

sentences.zh: 又以邠寧乏食，難於饋運，乃請軍於奉天。

translations.literal: Moreover, because Binning lacked food and supply transport was difficult, they requested to station the army at Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: Because Binning lacked grain and supply lines were strained, they asked to encamp the army at Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 是時公廩亦竭，縣吏憂恐多逃匿，群行剽盜，孝德不能禁。

translations.literal: At this time the public granaries were also exhausted; county clerks in fear and alarm mostly fled and hid; groups went about plundering and robbing, and Xiaode could not stop them.
translations.idiomatic: Public granaries were empty, county officials fled in panic, and bandits roamed in gangs; Xiaode could not suppress them.

sentences.zh: 秀實私曰：「使我為軍候，當不如此。

translations.literal: Xiushi said privately: 'If I were made army inspector, it would not be like this.'
translations.idiomatic: Xiushi remarked privately, "Put me in charge of discipline and this would not happen."

sentences.zh: 」軍司馬言之，遂以秀實為都虞候，權知奉天行營事，號令嚴一，軍府安泰，代宗聞而嗟賞久之。

translations.literal: ' The army marshal spoke of this, and thereupon Xiushi was made chief inspector, with provisional charge of the Fengtian field headquarters; orders were strict and uniform, the army headquarters secure and peaceful, and Daizong heard of it and sighed in admiration for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: " The army marshal relayed this, and Xiushi was appointed chief inspector with provisional authority over the Fengtian camp. His discipline was ironclad, order returned to headquarters, and Daizong heard of it with prolonged admiration.

sentences.zh: 兵還於邠寧，復為都虞候，尋拜涇州刺史。

translations.literal: When the army returned to Binning he again served as chief inspector, and soon was appointed prefect of Jing prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the troops returned to Binning he resumed as chief inspector and was soon appointed prefect of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 大曆元年，馬璘奏加開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dali, Ma Lin memorialized to add Grand Master with Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: In Dali year 1, Ma Lin was recommended for the honor of Grand Master with Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 軍中有能引二十四弓而犯盜者，璘欲免之，秀實曰：「將有私愛，則法令不一，雖韓、白復生，亦不能為理。

translations.literal: In the army there was one who could draw twenty-four bows and who had committed robbery; Lin wished to pardon him. Xiushi said: 'When a general has private favoritism, then laws and orders are not uniform; even if Han Xin and Bai Qi were reborn, they could not bring order.'
translations.idiomatic: A soldier who could draw twenty-four bows had been caught stealing; Lin wanted to spare him. Xiushi said, "When a commander plays favorites, the law loses its force—even Han Xin and Bai Qi reborn could not govern such an army."

sentences.zh: 」璘善其議，竟使殺之。

translations.literal: ' Lin approved his argument and in the end had him executed.
translations.idiomatic: " Lin accepted his reasoning and had the man executed.

sentences.zh: 璘決事有不合理者，必固爭之，得璘引過乃已。

translations.literal: When Lin decided affairs unreasonably, Xiushi would firmly dispute until Lin acknowledged his error and then stop.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Lin's decisions were unsound, Xiushi argued him down until Lin admitted his mistake.

sentences.zh: 璘城涇州，秀實掌留後，歸還，加御史中丞。

translations.literal: Lin walled Jing prefecture; Xiushi managed the rear headquarters; when Lin returned, Xiushi was made vice censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: While Lin fortified Jingzhou, Xiushi served as rear-area administrator; on Lin's return he was promoted to vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 璘既奉詔徙鎮涇州，其士眾嘗自四鎮、北庭赴難中原，僑居驟移，頗積勞怨。

translations.literal: After Lin received the edict to transfer his command to Jing prefecture, his soldiers and masses had once come from the Four Garrisons and Beiting to aid the Central Plains in crisis; sudden relocation in exile had accumulated much fatigue and resentment.
translations.idiomatic: When Lin was ordered to transfer his headquarters to Jingzhou, his troops—who had marched from the Four Garrisons and Beiting to save the empire—found themselves uprooted again and nursed deep grievances.

sentences.zh: 刀斧將王童之因人心動搖，導以為亂。

translations.literal: Axe-and-blade officer Wang Tongzhi, taking advantage of wavering hearts, led them toward rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The executioner officer Wang Tongzhi exploited the unrest to incite mutiny.

sentences.zh: 或告其事，且曰：「候嚴，警鼓為約矣。

translations.literal: Someone reported the matter and also said: 'They wait for the night watch to grow strict—the alarm drum is their signal.'
translations.idiomatic: An informant reported the plot, adding that they would rise when the night watch tightened, using the alarm drum as their signal.

sentences.zh: 」秀實乃召鼓人，陽怒失節，且戒之曰：「每更籌盡，必來報。

translations.literal: ' Xiushi thereupon summoned the drummer, feigning anger at his lapse, and also warned him: 'At the end of each watch period you must come and report.'
translations.idiomatic: " Xiushi summoned the drummer, rebuked him ostentatiously for negligence, and ordered him to report at the end of every watch.

sentences.zh: 」每白之，輒延數刻，四更畢而曙。

translations.literal: ' Each time he reported, Xiushi would delay several quarters; the fourth watch ended and dawn came.
translations.idiomatic: " Each time the man reported, Xiushi delayed the drum by several quarters until the fourth watch had passed and dawn broke.

sentences.zh: 既差互，童之亂不能作。

translations.literal: Once the schedule was disrupted, Tongzhi's rebellion could not take place.
translations.idiomatic: With the timing thrown off, Tongzhi's uprising never materialized.

sentences.zh: 明日，告者復曰：「今夜將焚草場，期救火者同作亂。

translations.literal: The next day the informant again said: 'Tonight they will burn the fodder yard, planning that those who come to fight the fire will rise together in disorder.'
translations.idiomatic: The next day the informant warned that the conspirators would set the fodder yard ablaze that night and use the fire brigade as cover for a mutiny.

sentences.zh: 」秀實使嚴加警備。

translations.literal: ' Xiushi had them strictly increase guard and preparation.
translations.idiomatic: " Xiushi tightened security throughout the camp.

sentences.zh: 夜半火發，乃使令於軍中曰：「救火者斬。

translations.literal: ' At midnight fire broke out; he then sent an order through the army saying: 'Whoever fights the fire will be beheaded.'
translations.idiomatic: " At midnight the fire broke out. He issued an army-wide order: "Anyone who fights the fire will be executed."

sentences.zh: 」童之居外營，請入救火，不許。

translations.literal: ' Tongzhi was in the outer camp and requested to enter to fight the fire; this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: " Tongzhi, stationed in the outer camp, asked permission to enter and fight the blaze; Xiushi refused.

sentences.zh: 明日斬之，捕殺其黨凡十余人以徇，曰：「敢後徙者族！

translations.literal: The next day he beheaded him, captured and killed his faction of more than ten men as a warning, and said: 'Whoever dares lag behind in the move—his clan will be destroyed!'
translations.idiomatic: The next day he executed Tongzhi, killed more than ten accomplices as a warning, and proclaimed, "Anyone who delays the transfer will be punished with extinction of his clan!"

sentences.zh: 」於是遷涇州。

translations.literal: ' Thereupon they moved to Jing prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: " The army then marched to Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 既至其理所，人煙夐絕，且無廩食。

translations.literal: When they reached its administrative seat, human habitation was utterly sparse, and there was no granary food.
translations.idiomatic: At the new headquarters the land was nearly deserted and there were no public stores of grain.

sentences.zh: 朝廷憂之，遂詔璘遙管鄭、潁二州，以贍涇原軍，俾秀實為留後，二州甚理。

translations.literal: The court was troubled by this and thereupon ordered Lin to oversee Zheng and Ying prefectures from afar to support the Jingyuan army, appointing Xiushi as rear administrator; the two prefectures were very well governed.
translations.idiomatic: The court, alarmed at the shortage, ordered Lin to draw supplies remotely from Zheng and Ying prefectures to feed the Jingyuan army, with Xiushi as rear administrator; he governed both districts admirably.

sentences.zh: 璘思其績用，又奏行軍司馬，兼都知兵馬使。

translations.literal: Lin considered his achievements and usefulness and again memorialized him as field marshal and concurrently overall commander of troops and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Impressed by his record, Lin recommended him as field marshal and overall commander of the army.

sentences.zh: 八年，吐蕃來寇，戰於鹽倉，我軍不利。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Tibetans came to raid; they fought at Yancang and our army fared poorly.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8 the Tibetans invaded; at Yancang our forces were defeated.

sentences.zh: 璘為寇戎所隔，逮暮未還，敗將潰兵爭道而入。

translations.literal: Lin was cut off by the enemy barbarians and by evening had not returned; defeated generals and routed soldiers fought for the road to enter.
translations.idiomatic: Lin was cut off by the enemy and failed to return by nightfall; routed officers and soldiers stampeded through the gates.

sentences.zh: 時都將焦令諶與諸將四五輩狼狽而至，秀實召讓之曰：「兵法：失將，麾下當斬。

translations.literal: At that time chief commander Jiao Lingchen and four or five other generals arrived in disarray; Xiushi summoned and rebuked them, saying: 'By the art of war, when the commander is lost, his subordinates should be beheaded.'
translations.idiomatic: Chief commander Jiao Lingchen and four or five other officers straggled in in disorder. Xiushi summoned them and rebuked them: "Military law demands that when the commander is lost, his subordinates pay with their lives."

sentences.zh: 公等忘其死而欲安其家耶！

translations.literal: Have you forgotten death yet wish to secure your families!'
translations.idiomatic: Have you forgotten your duty to die and seek only to save yourselves?"

sentences.zh: 」令諶等恐懼，下拜數十。

translations.literal: ' Lingchen and the others were terrified and prostrated themselves dozens of times.
translations.idiomatic: " They were terrified and kowtowed repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 秀實乃悉驅城中士卒未出戰者，使驍將統之，東依古原，列奇兵示賊將戰，且以收合敗亡。

translations.literal: Xiushi then drove out all soldiers in the city who had not gone to battle, had fierce generals command them, moved east to rely on the ancient plain, arrayed surprise troops to show the bandits they would fight, and thereby gathered the defeated and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Xiushi mustered every soldier in the city who had not yet fought, placed them under his best commanders, and drew up a screen of troops on the plain east of the city to feign readiness for battle, rallying the fugitives as he did so.

sentences.zh: 蕃眾望之，不敢逼。

translations.literal: The Tibetan masses saw this and did not dare press close.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetans sighted the formation and dared not advance.

sentences.zh: 及夜，璘方獲歸。

translations.literal: By night Lin at last was able to return.
translations.idiomatic: Lin did not make it back until nightfall.

sentences.zh: 十一年，璘疾甚，不能視事，請秀實攝節度副使兼左廂兵馬使。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Lin's illness was severe and he could not handle affairs; he requested that Xiushi act as deputy military commissioner and concurrently left-wing army commander.
translations.idiomatic: In year 11 Lin fell gravely ill and could not govern; he asked Xiushi to serve as acting deputy commissioner and commander of the left wing.

sentences.zh: 秀實乃以十將張羽飛為招召將，分兵按甲，以備非常。

translations.literal: Xiushi then made tenth-rank commander Zhang Yufei recruitment commander, divided troops and set armor, to guard against the unexpected.
translations.idiomatic: Xiushi appointed tenth-rank commander Zhang Yufei to muster the troops, deployed the army under arms, and prepared for any emergency.

sentences.zh: 璘卒，而軍中行哭赴喪事於內，李漢惠接賓客於外，非其親不得居喪側，族談離立者捕而囚之。

translations.literal: When Lin died, within the army they performed mourning and funeral rites; Li Hanhui received guests outside; those not kin could not stand at the mourning side; those who gathered in clan talk standing apart were seized and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: When Lin died, mourning was conducted within headquarters while Li Hanhui received guests at the gate. Only kin were allowed beside the bier; anyone who clustered in factional talk was arrested.

sentences.zh: 都虞候史廷幹、裨將崔珍張景華謀作亂，秀實乃送廷幹於京師，徙珍及景華外鎮，軍中遂定，不戮一人。

translations.literal: Chief inspector Shi Tinggan and staff generals Cui Zhen and Zhang Jinghua plotted disorder; Xiushi sent Tinggan to the capital and transferred Zhen and Jinghua to outer garrisons; the army was then settled without executing a single man.
translations.idiomatic: Chief inspector Shi Tinggan and staff generals Cui Zhen and Zhang Jinghua plotted a coup; Xiushi sent Tinggan to the capital and transferred Zhen and Jinghua to distant posts, restoring order without a single execution.

sentences.zh: 尋拜秀實涇州刺史、兼御史大夫，四鎮北庭行軍涇原鄭潁節度使。

translations.literal: Soon Xiushi was appointed prefect of Jing prefecture and concurrently chief censor, military commissioner of the Four Garrisons and Beiting field army for Jingyuan, Zheng, and Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Xiushi was soon appointed prefect of Jingzhou, chief censor, and military commissioner of the Jingyuan, Zheng, and Ying circuit of the Four Garrisons and Beiting field army.

sentences.zh: 三四年間，吐蕃不敢犯塞，清約率易，遠近稱之。

translations.literal: Within three or four years the Tibetans did not dare violate the frontier; he was pure, frugal, and unassuming, and near and far praised him.
translations.idiomatic: For three or four years the Tibetans did not raid the border. His austerity and simplicity won praise throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 非公會，不聽樂飲酒，私室無妓媵，無贏財，退公之後，端居靜慮而已。

translations.literal: Except at public gatherings he did not listen to music or drink wine; his private quarters had no singing girls or concubines, no surplus wealth; after leaving public duty he simply sat upright in quiet reflection.
translations.idiomatic: Outside official functions he neither listened to music nor drank wine; he kept no entertainers or concubines and amassed no private fortune; after office hours he sat alone in contemplation.

sentences.zh: 德宗嗣位，就加檢校禮部尚書、張掖郡王。

translations.literal: When Dezong succeeded the throne, he was at once made acting Minister of Rites and Prince of Zhangye commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong acceded, Xiushi was concurrently appointed acting Minister of Rites and Prince of Zhangye.

sentences.zh: 建中元年，宰相楊炎欲行元載舊志，築原州城，開陵陽渠，詔中使上聞，仍問秀實可否之狀。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianzhong, chief minister Yang Yan wished to carry out Yuan Zai's old plan—wall Yuan prefecture and open the Lingyang canal; an edict sent a palace envoy to report upward and also to ask Xiushi whether he approved.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianzhong year 1, chief minister Yang Yan sought to revive Yuan Zai's plan to fortify Yuanzhou and open the Lingyang canal. The emperor sent a palace envoy to report on the project and to ask Xiushi's opinion.

sentences.zh: 秀實以為方春不可興土功，請俟農隙。

translations.literal: Xiushi considered that in early spring one should not launch earthworks and requested to wait until a break in the farming season.
translations.idiomatic: Xiushi argued that spring was no season for corvée labor and asked that work wait until after the harvest.

sentences.zh: 炎以其沮己之謀，遂除司農卿，以邠寧節度李懷光兼涇原節度使，以事西拓。

translations.literal: Yan, because he obstructed his plan, thereupon removed him to Minister of Agriculture and made Binning commissioner Li Huai'guang concurrently Jingyuan commissioner to pursue expansion westward.
translations.idiomatic: Yan, resenting his opposition, transferred him to Minister of Agriculture and gave Binning commissioner Li Huai'guang the added post of Jingyuan commissioner to push the western expansion.

sentences.zh: 無何，劉文喜叛，亦不果城。

translations.literal: Before long Liu Wenxi rebelled, and the walling also did not come to fruition.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Liu Wenxi rebelled, and the fortification was never built.

sentences.zh: 四年，朱泚盜據宮闕，源休教泚偽迎鑾駕，陰濟逆誌。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Zhu Ci seized the palace by theft; Yuan Xiu taught Ci to feign welcoming the imperial carriage, secretly aiding his rebellious intent.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4, Zhu Ci seized the capital. Yuan Xiu urged him to stage a false welcome for the emperor while secretly advancing the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 泚乃遣其將韓旻領馬步三千疾趨奉天。

translations.literal: Ci then sent his general Han Min leading three thousand horse and foot in rapid march toward Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: Ci dispatched general Han Min with three thousand cavalry and infantry in a forced march on Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 時蒼黃之中，未有武備。

translations.literal: At that time amid sudden alarm there was as yet no military preparation.
translations.idiomatic: The court, caught off guard, had no defenses ready.

sentences.zh: 泚以秀實嘗為涇原節度，頗得士心，後罷兵權，以為蓄憤且久，必肯同惡，乃召與謀議。

translations.literal: Ci, because Xiushi had once been Jingyuan commissioner and had won soldiers' hearts, and later had been stripped of military power, thought he harbored resentment for a long time and would surely join in villainy, and thus summoned him to counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Ci believed that Xiushi—who had once commanded Jingyuan and won the soldiers' loyalty, then been stripped of his army—must nurse a long grievance and would join the rebellion; he summoned him to counsel.

sentences.zh: 秀實初詐從之，陰說大將劉海賓、何明禮、姚令言判官岐靈嶽同謀殺泚，以兵迎乘輿。

translations.literal: Xiushi at first pretended to follow him and secretly urged great generals Liu Haibin, He Mingli, and Yao Lingyan's staff judge Qi Lingyue to conspire to kill Ci and with troops welcome the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Xiushi feigned compliance while secretly persuading generals Liu Haibin and He Mingli and Yao Lingyan's aide Qi Lingyue to assassinate Ci and march to receive the emperor.

sentences.zh: 三人者，皆秀實夙所獎遇，遂皆許諾。

translations.literal: The three men had all long been encouraged and favored by Xiushi, and thus all promised.
translations.idiomatic: All three had long been in Xiushi's favor and gave their assent.

sentences.zh: 及韓旻追駕，秀實以為宗社之危，期於頃刻，乃使人走諭靈嶽，竊令言印。

translations.literal: When Han Min pursued the imperial carriage, Xiushi thought the peril to the altars of state would come in a moment; he sent a man running to instruct Lingyue and secretly to take Lingyan's seal.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Min was sent to pursue the emperor, Xiushi saw the dynasty's peril as imminent and dispatched a runner to Qi Lingyue to steal Yao Lingyan's seal.

sentences.zh: 不遂，乃倒用司農印印符以追兵。

translations.literal: This did not succeed, so he used the Minister of Agriculture seal upside down to stamp the tally ordering the troops recalled.
translations.idiomatic: When that failed, he stamped a recall order with the Minister of Agriculture seal applied upside down.

sentences.zh: 旻至駱驛得符，軍人亦莫辯其印文，惶遽而回。

translations.literal: Min reached Luoyi post station and received the tally; the soldiers also could not distinguish the seal script and returned in alarm and haste.
translations.idiomatic: Min received the order at Luoyi station; his men could not tell the seal was reversed and turned back in panic.

sentences.zh: 秀實謂海賓等曰：「旻之來，吾黨無遺類矣！

translations.literal: Xiushi said to Haibin and the others: 'With Min's coming, none of our party will be left!'
translations.idiomatic: Xiushi told Haibin and the others, "If Min reaches the emperor, our whole party is finished!"

sentences.zh: 我當直搏殺泚，不得則死，終不能向此賊稱臣。

translations.literal: I shall directly grapple and kill Ci; if I do not succeed then die—I can never bow to this bandit as subject.'
translations.idiomatic: I will strike Ci down with my own hands; if I fail I shall die—but I will never bow to this traitor."

sentences.zh: 」乃與海賓約，事急為繼，而令明禮應於外。

translations.literal: ' He then made a pact with Haibin that when the matter grew urgent he would follow up, and ordered Mingli to respond from outside.
translations.idiomatic: " He arranged with Haibin to follow up if the attempt failed and told Mingli to act from outside.

sentences.zh: 明日，泚召秀實議事，源休、姚令言、李忠臣、李子平皆在坐。

translations.literal: The next day Ci summoned Xiushi to discuss affairs; Yuan Xiu, Yao Lingyan, Li Zhongchen, and Li Ziping were all seated.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Ci called Xiushi to council with Yuan Xiu, Yao Lingyan, Li Zhongchen, and Li Ziping in attendance.

sentences.zh: 秀實戎服，與泚並膝，語至僭位，秀實勃然而起，執休腕奪其象笏，奮躍而前，唾泚面大罵曰：「狂賊，吾恨不斬汝萬段，我豈逐汝反耶！

translations.literal: Xiushi in military dress sat knee to knee with Ci; when talk reached usurping the throne, Xiushi rose in sudden fury, seized Xiu's wrist and snatched his ivory tablet, leaped forward, spat in Ci's face and loudly cursed: 'Mad bandit! I regret I cannot cut you into ten thousand pieces—would I follow you in rebellion!'
translations.idiomatic: Xiushi came in armor and sat beside Ci. When the talk turned to usurpation, he sprang up, seized Yuan Xiu's wrist, snatched his court tablet, and lunged at Ci, spitting in his face and shouting, "Traitor! I wish I could cut you to pieces—did you think I would join your rebellion?"

sentences.zh: 」遂擊之。

translations.literal: ' Thereupon he struck him.
translations.idiomatic: " He struck Ci down.

sentences.zh: 泚舉臂自捍，才中其顙，流血匍匐而走。

translations.literal: Ci raised his arm to defend himself; the blow just hit his forehead, blood flowed, and he crawled away on hands and knees.
translations.idiomatic: Ci threw up his arm to block the blow, which glanced off his forehead; bleeding, he crawled away.

sentences.zh: 兇徒愕然，初不敢動；

translations.literal: The villainous followers were stunned and at first did not dare move;
translations.idiomatic: The conspirators stood frozen and dared not move;

sentences.zh: 而海賓等不至，秀實乃曰：「我不同汝反，何不殺我！

translations.literal: but Haibin and the others did not arrive; Xiushi then said: 'I do not join you in rebellion—why not kill me!'
translations.idiomatic: but Haibin and the others never came. Xiushi cried, "I will not rebel with you—then kill me!"

sentences.zh: 」兇黨群至，遂遇害焉。

translations.literal: ' The villainous faction swarmed forward, and he thereupon met calamity.
translations.idiomatic: " The traitors rushed in and slew him.

sentences.zh: 海賓、明禮、靈嶽相次被殺。

translations.literal: Haibin, Mingli, and Lingyue were in succession killed.
translations.idiomatic: Haibin, Mingli, and Lingyue were executed in turn.

sentences.zh: 德宗在奉天聞其事，惜其委用不至，垂涕久之。

translations.literal: Dezong at Fengtian heard of the affair, regretted that his employment had not reached its fullest, and wept for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: At Fengtian, Dezong heard the news, lamented that he had not used Xiushi to his full capacity, and wept for a long while.

sentences.zh: 初，秀實見禁兵寡少，不足以備非常，乃上疏曰：「臣聞天子曰萬乘，諸侯日千乘，大夫曰百乘，此蓋以大制小，以十制一也。

translations.literal: Earlier, Xiushi saw that the forbidden troops were few and insufficient to guard against the unexpected; he submitted a memorial saying: 'Your servant has heard that the Son of Heaven is called ten thousand chariots, feudal lords a thousand chariots, grandees a hundred chariots—this is fundamentally using the large to control the small, using ten to control one.'
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, seeing how few and poorly trained the palace guard were, Xiushi memorialized: "I have read that the Son of Heaven commands ten thousand chariots, a feudal lord one thousand, a grandee one hundred—meaning that the greater rules the lesser and the many control the few."

sentences.zh: 尊君卑臣，強幹弱枝之義，在於此矣。

translations.literal: The meaning of honoring the ruler and lowering subjects, strengthening the trunk and weakening the branches, lies in this.
translations.idiomatic: The principle of exalting the sovereign, subordinating ministers, and strengthening the center while weakening the periphery rests on this foundation."

sentences.zh: 今外有不庭之虜，內有梗命之臣，竊觀禁兵不精，其數全少，卒有患難，將何待之！

translations.literal: Now outside there are unrestrained barbarians, inside there are subjects who resist orders; your servant observes in secret that the forbidden troops are not skilled and their numbers are altogether few—if suddenly there is trouble, what will we rely on!'
translations.idiomatic: Yet now barbarians defy us on the frontier and disobedient ministers plot within. I see that the palace guard is neither well trained nor numerous; if disaster strikes, what shall we depend on?"

sentences.zh: 且猛虎所以百獸畏者，為爪牙也。

translations.literal: Moreover, the reason the fierce tiger is feared by all beasts is because of its claws and fangs.
translations.idiomatic: A tiger inspires fear among beasts because of its claws and fangs."

sentences.zh: 若去其爪牙，則犬彘馬牛悉能為敵。

translations.literal: If its claws and fangs are removed, then dogs, pigs, horses, and oxen can all become its enemies.
translations.idiomatic: Strip away its claws and fangs, and even dogs and cattle can stand against it."

sentences.zh: 伏願少留聖慮，冀裨萬一。

translations.literal: Your servant humbly wishes that Your Sagely Attention be briefly retained, hoping to benefit the realm in the smallest measure.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to give this matter your attention, however slight the benefit may be."

sentences.zh: 」及涇原兵作亂，召神策六軍，遂無一人至者。

translations.literal: ' When the Jingyuan troops rebelled, the Shence Six Armies were summoned, and in the end not a single man came.
translations.idiomatic: " When the Jingyuan mutiny broke out, the Shence Six Armies were called up—and not one man answered.

sentences.zh: 秀實守節不二，竟歿於賊，其明略義烈如此。

translations.literal: Xiushi held to his integrity without wavering and in the end perished at the hands of bandits—his clarity of strategy and righteous valor were thus.
translations.idiomatic: Xiushi held firm to his loyalty and died at the rebels' hands; such was his foresight and heroic devotion.

sentences.zh: 興元元年二月，詔曰：「見危致命之謂忠，臨義有勇之謂烈。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Xingyuan, an edict said: 'Facing peril and giving one's life is called loyalty; facing righteousness with courage is called valor.'
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Xingyuan year 1, an edict proclaimed: "To face danger and give one's life is loyalty; to face duty with courage is valor."

sentences.zh: 惟爾勵臣節，不憚殺身；

translations.literal: You alone urged on the integrity of a subject and did not fear giving your life;
translations.idiomatic: You alone upheld the integrity of a loyal servant and did not shrink from death;

sentences.zh: 惟予式嘉乃勛，懋昭大典。

translations.literal: I alone shall greatly praise your merit and splendidly proclaim the great rites.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore praise your merit and proclaim it in the grand rites of state.

sentences.zh: 曰臺不德，罔克若天，遘茲殷憂，變起都邑。

translations.literal: The throne lacks virtue and cannot accord with Heaven; we have encountered this deep sorrow, and upheaval has arisen in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The throne has fallen short of virtue and cannot match Heaven's mandate; deep calamity has struck and rebellion has convulsed the capital.

sentences.zh: 惟爾卿士，嗷然靡依，逼畏所加，淄澠共混。

translations.literal: You ministers and grandees howled with none to rely on; coercion and fear were applied, and the Zi and Sheng rivers flowed together undistinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers and officials cried out with nowhere to turn; under coercion and fear, right and wrong were confounded alike.

sentences.zh: 故開府儀同三司、檢校禮部尚書、兼司農卿、上柱國、張掖郡王段秀實，操行嶽立，忠厚精至，義形於色，勇必有仁。

translations.literal: The late Grand Master with Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon, acting Minister of Rites, concurrent Minister of Agriculture, Supreme Pillar of State, and Prince of Zhangye commandery Duan Xiushi—his conduct stood like a mountain peak, his loyalty and honesty were refined to the utmost, righteousness showed in his countenance, and his courage always contained benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: The late Grand Master Duan Xiushi, acting Minister of Rites and concurrent Minister of Agriculture, Supreme Pillar of State and Prince of Zhangye—his conduct stood like a mountain, his loyalty ran deep, righteousness showed in his face, and his courage was always tempered by humanity.

sentences.zh: 頃者嘗鎮涇原，克著威惠，叛卒知訓，咨爾以誠。

translations.literal: Recently he had governed Jingyuan, excelling in both awe and kindness; mutinous soldiers knew discipline and consulted you with sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: He had lately governed Jingyuan with a reputation for stern justice and kindness; the mutineers knew his discipline and turned to you in good faith.

sentences.zh: 賊泚藏奸，欺爾以詐。

translations.literal: The bandit Ci hid treachery and deceived you with fraud.
translations.idiomatic: The traitor Zhu Ci concealed his treachery and lured you with deceit.

sentences.zh: 守人臣之大節，見元惡之深情，端委國門，挺身白刃。

translations.literal: He kept the great integrity of a subject, beheld the chief villain's true nature, straightened his robes at the state gate, and thrust himself against naked blades.
translations.idiomatic: He upheld a subject's highest duty, saw through the arch-villain, arrayed himself at the palace gate, and threw himself against drawn steel.

sentences.zh: 誓碎兇渠之首，以敵君父之仇，視死如歸，履虎致咥。

translations.literal: He swore to smash the chief villain's head to answer the sovereign father's enmity, regarded death as returning home, and trod on tigers until they bit.
translations.idiomatic: He swore to strike down the rebel leader to avenge his sovereign, welcomed death as homecoming, and walked among tigers unafraid.

sentences.zh: 噫，天未悔禍，事乖垂成，雄風壯圖，振駭群盜。

translations.literal: Alas, Heaven had not yet turned from calamity; the affair fell short at the verge of success; his heroic wind and bold design shook and terrified the band of robbers.
translations.idiomatic: Alas, Heaven had not yet lifted the curse; success slipped from his grasp; yet his heroic spirit struck terror into the rebels.

sentences.zh: 昔王蠋守死以全節，周顗正色而抗詞，惟我信臣，無愧前哲。

translations.literal: Of old Wang Shu died holding his post to preserve integrity; Zhou Yi showed stern countenance and resisted with words—our faithful subject alone need not blush before the sages of the past.
translations.idiomatic: Of old Wang Shu died to preserve his integrity and Zhou Yi faced down tyranny with stern words—our faithful servant stands unashamed beside these sages.

sentences.zh: 聲震寰宇，義冠古今，足以激勵人倫，光昭史冊。

translations.literal: His fame shook the universe, his righteousness crowned past and present, sufficient to stir human relations and shine forth in the historical records.
translations.idiomatic: His fame resounds through the realm, his righteousness crowns all ages, and he shall inspire humanity and shine forever in history.

sentences.zh: 不有殊等之賞，孰表非常之功。

translations.literal: Without an extraordinary reward, who could display an uncommon achievement?
translations.idiomatic: Without extraordinary reward, how can uncommon merit be displayed?

sentences.zh: 爰議疇庸，特超檢限，著之甲令，樹此風聲。

translations.literal: Therefore we deliberate on ranking merit, specially exceeding the usual limits, inscribe it in the statutes, and plant this reputation as a model.
translations.idiomatic: We therefore rank his merit above ordinary limits, inscribe it in the statutes, and set this example for posterity.

sentences.zh: 可贈太尉，謚曰忠烈，宣付史官，仍賜實封五百戶、莊宅各一區。

translations.literal: He may be posthumously made Grand Commandant, posthumous title Loyal and Valiant, proclaimed to the historiographers, and additionally granted five hundred actual households and one estate each.
translations.idiomatic: He is posthumously appointed Grand Commandant with the posthumous title Loyal and Valiant; the historiographers are to record this, and five hundred enfeoffed households plus an estate are granted.

sentences.zh: 長子與三品正員官，諸子並與五品正員官。

translations.literal: His eldest son is granted a regular third-rank post; all sons are granted regular fifth-rank posts.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son is granted a regular third-rank office; all other sons receive regular fifth-rank offices.

sentences.zh: 仍廢朝三日，收京城之後，以禮葬祭，旌表門閭。

translations.literal: Court is additionally suspended for three days; after recovering the capital, bury and sacrifice according to rites and honor his gate and lane.
translations.idiomatic: Court mourning is observed for three days; after the capital is recovered, he shall receive full rites of burial and sacrifice, and his household shall be publicly honored.

sentences.zh: 朕承天子人，臨馭億兆，一夫不獲，時予之辜，況誠信不達，屢致寇戎，使抱義之臣陷於兇逆。

translations.literal: We inherit the Son of Heaven's mandate and oversee hundreds of millions; if one man is not provided for, it is Our fault in season—how much more when sincerity and trust do not reach through, repeatedly bringing enemy barbarians, causing subjects who embraced righteousness to fall into villainous rebels.
translations.idiomatic: We bear Heaven's mandate over the multitude; if a single man goes without, the fault is Ours—how much worse when trust fails and invaders come again and again, casting loyal men into the hands of traitors.

sentences.zh: 有臨危致命，歿而逾彰；

translations.literal: There are those who face peril and give their lives, whose fame grows greater after death;
translations.idiomatic: Some face peril and give their lives, growing more glorious in death;

sentences.zh: 有因事成功，權以合道。

translations.literal: there are those who succeed through events and bend authority to accord with the Way;
translations.idiomatic: others achieve success in crisis and bend expedience to the right path;

sentences.zh: 茍利社稷，存亡一致，酬報之典，豈限常倫。

translations.literal: if it profits the altars of state, survival and destruction are one; the canon of recompense—how could it be limited by ordinary norms?
translations.idiomatic: when the state benefits, life and death are one; rewards for such service cannot be bound by ordinary rules.

sentences.zh: 並委所司訪其事跡，續具條奏，當加褒異，錫其井賦。

translations.literal: All are entrusted to the relevant offices to investigate their deeds, to continue submitting detailed memorials item by item; they shall receive special praise and be granted well-field revenues.
translations.idiomatic: Let the relevant offices investigate such cases and report in detail; exceptional honors shall be granted, including well-field revenues.

sentences.zh: 圖形雲閣，書功鼎彜，以彰我有服節死義之臣，傳於不朽。

translations.literal: Portraits in the Cloud Tower, achievements inscribed on tripods and cauldrons—to display that We have subjects who upheld integrity and died for righteousness, transmitted to immortality.
translations.idiomatic: Their portraits shall hang in the Cloud Tower and their deeds be cast on bronze vessels, so that Our loyal servants who died for righteousness shall live forever."

sentences.zh: 」德宗還京，又詔曰：「贈太尉秀實，授乎貞烈，激其頹風，蒼黃之中，密蘊雄斷。

translations.literal: ' When Dezong returned to the capital, another edict said: 'The posthumous Grand Commandant Xiushi was endowed with steadfast valor, stirred the declining wind; amid sudden alarm he secretly harbored heroic resolve.
translations.idiomatic: " When Dezong returned to Chang'an, another edict read: "The posthumously appointed Grand Commandant Xiushi embodied steadfast valor and roused a failing age; amid sudden crisis he concealed a heroic resolve.

sentences.zh: 將紓國難，詭收寇兵，撓其兇謀，果集吾事。

translations.literal: He was about to relieve the state's peril, deceptively recalled the rebel troops, thwarted their villainous plot, and truly gathered Our cause.
translations.idiomatic: He sought to save the dynasty, deceived the rebel forces into turning back, disrupted their plot, and brought Our cause to fruition.

sentences.zh: 挺身徑進，奮擊渠魁，英名凜然，振邁千古。

translations.literal: He thrust his body straight forward, struck fiercely at the ringleader; his heroic name was stern and awe-inspiring, shaking and surpassing a thousand ages.
translations.idiomatic: He charged forward and struck at the rebel leader; his heroic name stands awe-inspiring, resounding through the ages.

sentences.zh: 宜差官致祭，並旌表門閭，緣葬所須，一切官給。

translations.literal: Officials should be dispatched to perform sacrifices, and his gate and lane honored; all needs for the funeral shall be supplied by the state.
translations.idiomatic: Officials shall be sent to perform sacrifices; his household shall be honored; all funeral expenses shall be provided by the state.

sentences.zh: 仍於墓所官為立碑，以揚徽烈。

translations.literal: Additionally at the tomb site the state shall erect a stele to spread his fine valor.
translations.idiomatic: A state stele shall be erected at his tomb to proclaim his glory."

sentences.zh: 」自貞元後累朝凡赦書節文褒獎忠烈，必以秀實為首。

translations.literal: ' From Zhenyuan onward, through successive reigns, whenever amnesty documents and festival texts praised loyal valor, Xiushi was always placed first.
translations.idiomatic: " From the Zhenyuan era onward, whenever amnesties and festival proclamations praised loyal martyrs, Xiushi was always named first.

sentences.zh: 其子伯倫，累官至太子詹事。

translations.literal: His son Bolun rose through offices to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bolun rose to the post of Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 大和二年正月奏：「亡父贈太尉秀實，準前後制敕令所司置廟立碑，今營造已畢，取今月二十五日行升祔禮。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year of Dahe he memorialized: 'My deceased father, posthumous Grand Commandant Xiushi, according to prior and subsequent regulations and edicts ordering the offices to establish a temple and erect a stele—construction is now complete; we request the twenty-fifth of this month to perform the rite of elevating the tablet and enshrining the spirit.'
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Dahe year 2 he memorialized: "My late father, posthumous Grand Commandant Xiushi, was by prior edicts to receive a temple and stele. Construction is complete; we request the enshrinement rite on the twenty-fifth of this month."

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「秀實忠衛宗社，功配廟食，義風所激，千載凜然。

translations.literal: ' An edict said: 'Xiushi loyally guarded the altars of state; his merit matches temple offerings; the wind of righteousness he stirred remains stern through a thousand years.'
translations.idiomatic: " The edict replied: "Xiushi loyally defended the altars of state; his merit warrants temple sacrifice; the moral force he embodied remains awe-inspiring after a thousand years."

sentences.zh: 間代勛力，須異等夷，宜賜綾絹五百疋，以度支物充。

translations.literal: Merit spanning generations requires a reward of special rank; he should be granted five hundred bolts of silk damask, supplied from the revenue office stores.
translations.idiomatic: Merit of this order requires exceptional reward: grant five hundred bolts of silk from the revenue office stores.

sentences.zh: 仍令所司供少牢，並給鹵簿人夫，兼太常博士一人檢校。

translations.literal: Additionally order the relevant offices to supply the lesser livestock sacrifice, provide imperial guard escort and laborers, and assign one Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to supervise.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant offices shall supply sacrificial victims, provide imperial escort and attendants, and assign one Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to supervise."

sentences.zh: 」尋加伯倫檢校左散騎常侍，兼殿中監。

translations.literal: ' Soon Bolun was additionally made acting Left Regular Attendant and concurrent Supervisor of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: " Bolun was soon appointed acting Left Regular Attendant and concurrent Supervisor of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 大和四年十一月，遷右金吾衛大將軍、兼御史大夫，充街使。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the fourth year of Dahe he was transferred to Great General of the Right Gold Crow Guard, concurrently Chief Censor, and appointed street commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Dahe year 4 he was made Great General of the Right Gold Crow Guard, concurrent Chief Censor, and street commissioner.

sentences.zh: 八年七月，檢校工部尚書，充福建等州都團練觀察使，入為太仆卿，卒。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the eighth year he was made acting Minister of Works and appointed overall training and observation commissioner of Fujian and other prefectures; he entered the capital as Minister of the Stud and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of year 8 he was appointed acting Minister of Works and commissioner of Fujian; he later entered the capital as Minister of the Stud and died.

sentences.zh: 宰臣李石奏曰：「伯倫，秀實之子。

translations.literal: Chief minister Li Shi memorialized: 'Bolun is Xiushi's son.'
translations.idiomatic: Chief minister Li Shi reported: "Bolun was Xiushi's son."

sentences.zh: 自古歿身以衛社稷者，無如秀實之賢。

translations.literal: From antiquity among those who gave their lives to guard the altars of state, none matched Xiushi in worth.
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity, none who gave his life for the state matched Xiushi in worth."

sentences.zh: 」文宗憫然曰：「伯倫宜加賻贈。

translations.literal: ' Wenzong said with compassion: 'Bolun should receive additional funeral gifts.'
translations.idiomatic: " Wenzong said with compassion, "Bolun should receive additional funeral gifts."

sentences.zh: 」仍輟朝一日，以禮忠臣之嗣。

translations.literal: ' Court was additionally suspended for one day to honor the heir of a loyal subject.
translations.idiomatic: " Court was suspended for one day in honor of the loyal servant's heir.

sentences.zh: 顏真卿顏真卿，字清臣，瑯邪臨沂人也。

translations.literal: Yan Zhenqing, Yan Zhenqing, courtesy name Qingchen, was a native of Linyi in Langye.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhenqing, whose courtesy name was Qingchen, came from Linyi in Langye.

sentences.zh: 五代祖之推，北齊黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: His fifth-generation ancestor Zhitui was a Yellow Gate Attendant of Northern Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His fifth-generation ancestor Zhitui had been a Yellow Gate Attendant of Northern Qi.

sentences.zh: 真卿少勤學業，有詞藻，尤工書。

translations.literal: Zhenqing in youth diligently pursued learning, had literary talent, and was especially skilled at calligraphy.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Zhenqing studied diligently, showed literary talent, and excelled at calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 開元中，舉進士，登甲科。

translations.literal: During Kaiyuan he took the jinshi examination and passed in the top class.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaiyuan reign he passed the jinshi examination in the top class.

sentences.zh: 事親以孝聞。

translations.literal: He was known for filial service to his parents.
translations.idiomatic: He was renowned for filial devotion to his parents.

sentences.zh: 四命為監察御史，充河西隴右軍試覆屯交兵使。

translations.literal: Four times he was appointed investigating censor and served as trial reviewer of garrison and supply disputes for the Hexi and Longyou armies.
translations.idiomatic: He was four times appointed investigating censor and served as trial reviewer of garrison and supply disputes for the Hexi and Longyou armies.

sentences.zh: 五原有冤獄，久不決，真卿至，立辯之。

translations.literal: At Wuyuan there was a wrongful case long unresolved; when Zhenqing arrived, he immediately argued it through.
translations.idiomatic: At Wuyuan a wrongful case had languished unresolved; Zhenqing arrived and settled it at once.

sentences.zh: 天方旱，獄決乃雨，郡人呼之為「御史雨」。

translations.literal: Heaven was then in drought; when the case was decided rain fell, and the commandery people called it 'the Censor's Rain.'
translations.idiomatic: The region was in drought; rain fell when the case was resolved, and the people called it "the Censor's Rain."

sentences.zh: 又充河東朔方試覆屯交兵使。

translations.literal: He also served as trial reviewer for the Hedong and Shuofang armies.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as trial reviewer for the Hedong and Shuofang armies.

sentences.zh: 有鄭延祚者，母卒二十九年，殯僧舍垣地，真卿劾奏之，兄弟三十年不齒，天下聳動。

translations.literal: There was one Zheng Yanzuo whose mother had died twenty-nine years before but was coffined in a monk's quarters by the wall; Zhenqing impeached and memorialized this; the brothers had not been received in society for thirty years—the realm was shaken.
translations.idiomatic: When Zheng Yanzuo had left his mother's coffin in a monastery wall for twenty-nine years, Zhenqing impeached him; the brothers had been ostracized for thirty years, and the whole empire took notice.

sentences.zh: 遷殿中侍御史、東都畿采訪判官，轉侍御史、武部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to palace attendant censor and Eastern Capital metropolitan circuit investigation staff judge, then to attendant censor and vice director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to palace censor and Eastern Capital investigation staff judge, then to attendant censor and vice director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 楊國忠怒其不附己，出為平原太守。

translations.literal: Yang Guozhong was angry that he would not attach himself to him and sent him out as prefect of Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guozhong, angered that he would not ally with him, posted him out as prefect of Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 安祿山逆節頗著，真卿以霖雨為托，修城浚池，陰料丁壯，儲廩實，乃陽會文士，泛舟外池，飲酒賦詩。

translations.literal: An Lushan's rebellious conduct was quite evident; Zhenqing used heavy rains as a pretext to repair walls and dredge moats, secretly mustered able-bodied men and stored granary grain, then openly gathered literati, boated on the outer pond, and drank wine composing verse.
translations.idiomatic: As An Lushan's treason became plain, Zhenqing used seasonal rains as a cover to repair walls, dredge moats, secretly muster men, and fill granaries, while openly hosting literati for boating, wine, and poetry on the outer pond.

sentences.zh: 或讒於祿山，祿山亦密偵之，以為書生不足虞也。

translations.literal: Some slandered him to Lushan; Lushan also secretly spied on him and thought a bookish man was not worth worrying about.
translations.idiomatic: Some informed on him to Lushan, who also had him watched but dismissed him as a harmless scholar.

sentences.zh: 無幾，祿山果反，河朔盡陷，獨平原城守具備，乃使司兵參軍李平馳奏之。

translations.literal: Before long Lushan indeed rebelled; north of the Yellow River all fell, only Pingyuan's defenses were complete, and he sent army staff officer Li Ping in rapid dispatch to memorialize this.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Lushan rebelled and all Hebei fell—only Pingyuan stood ready. Zhenqing sent staff officer Li Ping in urgent report to the throne.

sentences.zh: 玄宗初聞祿山之變，嘆曰：「河北二十四郡，豈無一忠臣乎！

translations.literal: When Xuanzong first heard of Lushan's upheaval he sighed: 'Of the twenty-four commanderies of Hebei, can there not be a single loyal subject!'
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong first heard of the rebellion he sighed, "Among the twenty-four commanderies of Hebei, is there not one loyal man?"

sentences.zh: 」得平來，大喜，顧左右曰：「朕不識顏真卿形狀何如，所為得如此！

translations.literal: ' When Ping came he was greatly pleased and said to those beside him: 'We do not know what Yan Zhenqing looks like, yet his deeds reach such heights!'
translations.idiomatic: " When Ping arrived the emperor rejoiced and said to his attendants, "I do not even know what Yan Zhenqing looks like, yet he has done this!"

sentences.zh: 」祿山初尚移牒真卿，令以平原、博平軍屯七千人防河津，以博平太守張獻直為副。

translations.literal: ' At first Lushan still sent dispatches to Zhenqing ordering him to station seven thousand troops of the Pingyuan and Boping armies to guard the river crossings, with Boping prefect Zhang Xianzhi as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: " Lushan at first still sent orders for Zhenqing to post seven thousand men from Pingyuan and Boping to guard the river crossings, with Boping prefect Zhang Xianzhi as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 真卿乃募勇士，旬日得萬人，遣錄事參軍李擇交統之簡閱，以刁萬歲、和琳、徐浩、馬相如、高抗朗等為將。

translations.literal: Zhenqing then recruited brave warriors and in ten days obtained ten thousand men, sent recorder Li Zejiao to command their review and inspection, and made Diao Wansui, He Lin, Xu Hao, Ma Xiangru, Gao Kanglang, and others generals.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenqing recruited ten thousand warriors in ten days, put recorder Li Zejiao in charge of their training, and appointed Diao Wansui, He Lin, Xu Hao, Ma Xiangru, Gao Kanglang, and others as generals.

sentences.zh: 祿山既陷洛陽，殺留守李憕、御史中丞盧奕、判官蔣清，以三首遣叚子光來徇河北。

translations.literal: After Lushan took Luoyang he killed garrison commander Li Guang, chief censor Lu Yi, and staff judge Jiang Qing, and sent the three heads with Duan Ziguang to display through Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: After Lushan captured Luoyang he killed garrison commander Li Guang, chief censor Lu Yi, and staff judge Jiang Qing, and sent their heads with Duan Ziguang to intimidate Hebei.

sentences.zh: 真卿恐搖人心，乃許謂諸將曰：「我識此三人，首皆非也。

translations.literal: Zhenqing feared to shake men's hearts and therefore pretended to tell the generals: 'I recognize these three men—the heads are not theirs.'
translations.idiomatic: Fearing panic among his men, Zhenqing told the generals, "I knew these three men—these are not their heads."

sentences.zh: 」遂腰斬子光，密藏三首。

translations.literal: ' He then cut Ziguang in two at the waist and secretly hid the three heads.
translations.idiomatic: " He had Ziguang cut in two at the waist and secretly preserved the three heads.

sentences.zh: 異日，乃取三首冠飾，草續支體，棺斂祭殯，為位慟哭，人心益附。

translations.literal: Another day he took the three heads, crowned and adorned them, used straw to complete the limbs, coffined and buried them with sacrifice, set up positions and wept bitterly—hearts attached to him still more.
translations.idiomatic: Later he restored the heads with proper adornment, supplied straw limbs, gave them full burial rites, and wept before their spirit tablets; loyalty to him deepened.

sentences.zh: 祿山遣其將李欽溱、高邈、何千年等守土門。

translations.literal: Lushan sent his generals Li Qin'an, Gao Miao, He Qiannian, and others to hold Tumen Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan posted generals Li Qin'an, Gao Miao, He Qiannian, and others to hold Tumen Pass.

sentences.zh: 真卿從父兄常山太守杲卿與長史袁履謙謀殺溱、邈，擒千年送京師。

translations.literal: Zhenqing's paternal cousin by descent, Changshan prefect Gao Qing, with chief administrator Yuan Lüqian plotted to kill Qin'an and Miao and captured Qiannian to send to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenqing's cousin Gao Qing, prefect of Changshan, and chief administrator Yuan Lüqian killed Qin'an and Miao and sent He Qiannian captive to the capital.

sentences.zh: 土門既開，十七郡同日歸順，共推真卿為帥，得兵二十余萬，橫絕燕、趙。

translations.literal: Once Tumen was opened, seventeen commanderies on the same day submitted; together they promoted Zhenqing as commander, obtained more than two hundred thousand troops, and cut across Yan and Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: With Tumen opened, seventeen commanderies submitted the same day and chose Zhenqing as their leader, raising more than two hundred thousand men who blocked the rebels across Yan and Zhao.

sentences.zh: 詔加真卿戶部侍郎，依前平原太守。

translations.literal: An edict added Zhenqing as vice director of the Ministry of Revenue while retaining him as before as prefect of Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed vice director of the Ministry of Revenue while retaining his post as prefect of Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 清河客李㟧，年二十余，與郡人來乞師，謂真卿曰：「聞公義烈，首唱大順，河朔諸郡恃公為長城。

translations.literal: A Qinghe traveler, Li Mo, aged a little over twenty, came with men of the commandery to beg for troops and said to Zhenqing: 'I have heard of your lordship's righteous valor, first raising the great cause of restoration; the commanderies north of the Yellow River rely on you as their Great Wall.'
translations.idiomatic: Li Mo of Qinghe, barely twenty, came with local men to request troops and told Zhenqing, "Your righteous leadership has launched the restoration; the Hebei commanderies look to you as their bulwark."

sentences.zh: 今清河，實公之西鄰也，僕幸寓家，得其虛實，知可為長者用。

translations.literal: Now Qinghe is truly your western neighbor; your servant has fortunately lodged there and knows its true condition, and knows it can serve the elder's use.'
translations.idiomatic: Qinghe is your western neighbor; I have lived there and know its strengths—it can serve your purpose."

sentences.zh: 今計其蓄積，足以三平原之富，士卒可以二平原之強。

translations.literal: Now estimating its stores, they are sufficient for three times Pingyuan's wealth; soldiers can match twice Pingyuan's strength.
translations.idiomatic: Its stores are three times those of Pingyuan and its troops twice as strong.

sentences.zh: 公因而撫之，腹心輔車之郡，其他小城，運之如臂使指耳。

translations.literal: If your lordship thereupon wins them over, it will be a commandery close as heart and chariot-wheel hub; other small cities will be moved as if the arm directed the fingers.
translations.idiomatic: Win it over and you gain a vital ally; the lesser towns will follow as the arm moves the fingers."

sentences.zh: 唯公所意，誰敢不從。

translations.literal: Whatever your lordship intends, who would dare not follow?
translations.idiomatic: Whatever you command, who would refuse?"

sentences.zh: 」真卿借兵千人。

translations.literal: ' Zhenqing lent him a thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhenqing lent him a thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 㟧將去，真卿謂之曰：「兵出也，吾子何以教我？

translations.literal: As Mo was about to leave, Zhenqing said to him: 'The troops are setting out—how would you instruct me?'
translations.idiomatic: As Mo was leaving, Zhenqing asked, "The troops are marching—what counsel do you offer?"

sentences.zh: 」㟧曰：「今聞朝廷使程千里統眾十萬自太行東下，將出𡻳口，為賊所扼，兵不得前。

translations.literal: ' Mo said: 'Now I hear the court has sent Cheng Qianli commanding a hundred thousand men eastward down the Taihang range, about to emerge at Lukou, but they are blocked by bandits and the army cannot advance.'
translations.idiomatic: " Mo replied, "The court has sent Cheng Qianli with a hundred thousand men down the Taihang toward Lukou, but the rebels hold the pass and he cannot advance."

sentences.zh: 今若先伐魏郡，斬袁知泰，太守司馬垂使為西南主；

translations.literal: If we now first attack Wei commandery, behead Yuan Zhita, and make prefect Sima Chui the southwest commander;
translations.idiomatic: First strike Wei commandery, kill Yuan Zhita, and make prefect Sima Chui commander of the southwest;

sentences.zh: 分兵開𡻳口之路，出千里之兵使討鄴、幽陵；

translations.literal: divide troops to open the Lukou road and release Qianli's army to campaign against Ye and Youling;
translations.idiomatic: send a detachment to open Lukou and free Qianli's army to attack Ye and Youling;

sentences.zh: 平原、清河合同志十萬之眾徇洛陽，分兵而制其衝。

translations.literal: Pingyuan and Qinghe together with allies field a hundred thousand to march on Luoyang and divide troops to control their strategic points.
translations.idiomatic: Pingyuan and Qinghe with a hundred thousand allies march on Luoyang while detachments hold the strategic crossings."

sentences.zh: 計王師亦不下十萬，公當堅壁，無與挑戰，不數十日，賊必潰而相圖矣。

translations.literal: Counting the imperial army as no less than a hundred thousand, your lordship should hold firm walls and not offer battle; within not many tens of days the bandits will surely collapse and turn on one another.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial army numbers at least a hundred thousand. Hold your walls and avoid battle; within ten days the rebels will collapse and turn on each other."

sentences.zh: 」真卿然之，乃移牒清河等郡，遣其大將李擇交、副將平原縣令范東馥、裨將和琳、徐浩等進兵，與清河四千人合勢，而博平以千人來，三郡之師屯於博平，去堂邑縣西南十里。

translations.literal: ' Zhenqing approved this, sent dispatches to Qinghe and other commanderies, dispatched his great general Li Zejiao, deputy general Pingyuan county magistrate Fan Dongfu, staff generals He Lin, Xu Hao, and others to advance, combined strength with Qinghe's four thousand men, and Boping sent a thousand; the three commanderies' armies encamped at Boping, ten li southwest of Tangyi county.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhenqing agreed, summoned Qinghe and neighboring districts, and sent Li Zejiao, Fan Dongfu, He Lin, and Xu Hao forward. With four thousand from Qinghe and a thousand from Boping, the allied force encamped at Boping, ten li southwest of Tangyi.

sentences.zh: 袁知泰遣其將白嗣深、乙舒蒙等以二萬人來拒戰，賊大敗，斬首萬余級。

translations.literal: Yuan Zhita sent his generals Bai Sishen, Yi Shumeng, and others with twenty thousand men to resist battle; the bandits were greatly defeated and more than ten thousand heads were cut.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zhita sent Bai Sishen and Yi Shumeng with twenty thousand men to meet them; the rebels were routed and more than ten thousand were beheaded.

sentences.zh: 肅宗幸靈武，授工部尚書、兼御史大夫、河北采訪招討使。

translations.literal: Suzong proceeded to Lingwu and appointed him Minister of Works, concurrently Chief Censor, and Hebei investigation and suppression commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Suzong reached Lingwu he appointed Zhenqing Minister of Works, concurrent Chief Censor, and Hebei investigation and suppression commissioner.

sentences.zh: 祿山乘虛遣史思明、尹子奇急攻河北諸郡，饒陽、河間、景城、東安相次陷沒，獨平原、博平、清河三郡城守，然人心危盪，不可復振。

translations.literal: Lushan seized the opportunity to send Shi Siming and Yin Ziqi in rapid attack on the Hebei commanderies; Raoyang, Hejian, Jingcheng, and Dong'an fell in succession; only Pingyuan, Boping, and Qinghe three commanderies held their walls, yet hearts were perilously shaken and could not be rallied again.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan sent Shi Siming and Yin Ziqi in a swift offensive; Raoyang, Hejian, Jingcheng, and Dong'an fell in turn. Only Pingyuan, Boping, and Qinghe still held out, but morale collapsed beyond recovery.

sentences.zh: 至德元年十月，棄郡渡河，歷江淮、荊襄。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the first year of Zhide he abandoned the commandery, crossed the river, and passed through Jiang-Huai, Jing, and Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Zhide year 1 he abandoned his post, crossed the river, and traveled through the Jiang-Huai and Jing-Xiang regions.

sentences.zh: 二年四月，朝於鳳翔，授憲部尚書，尋加御史大夫。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year he had audience at Fengxiang, was appointed Minister of Justice, and soon made Chief Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of year 2 he had audience at Fengxiang and was appointed Minister of Justice, soon also Chief Censor.

sentences.zh: 中書舍人兼吏部侍郎崔漪帶酒容入朝，諫議大夫李何忌在班不肅，真卿劾之；

translations.literal: Palace Secretariat drafter and concurrent vice director of the Ministry of Personnel Cui Yi entered court with a drunken appearance; remonstrance grandee Li Heji was in the ranks without decorum—Zhenqing impeached them;
translations.idiomatic: Palace drafter and vice director of Personnel Cui Yi appeared drunk at court; remonstrance grandee Li Heji behaved improperly in the ranks—Zhenqing impeached them;

sentences.zh: 貶漪為右庶子，何忌西平郡司馬。

translations.literal: Yi was demoted to Right Vice Heir Apparent, Heji to Xiping commandery secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yi was demoted to Right Vice Heir Apparent and Li Heji to secretary of Xiping commandery.

sentences.zh: 元帥廣平王領朔方蕃漢兵號二十萬來收長安，出辭之日，百僚致謁於朝堂。

translations.literal: Marshal the Prince of Guangping led Shuofang barbarian and Han troops said to number two hundred thousand to recover Chang'an; on the day of his departure farewell, the hundred officials came to pay respects in the court hall.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Guangping led two hundred thousand Shuofang and Han troops to recover Chang'an; on the day of his departure the officials came to pay their respects in court.

sentences.zh: 百僚拜，答拜，辭亦如之。

translations.literal: The hundred officials bowed, he returned the bows, and at farewell it was likewise.
translations.idiomatic: The officials bowed; he returned their bows; the farewell followed the same form.

sentences.zh: 王當闕不乘馬，步出木馬門而後乘。

translations.literal: The prince, facing the palace gate, did not mount a horse, walked out through the Wooden Horse Gate and only then mounted.
translations.idiomatic: Before the palace gate the prince did not mount but walked out through the Wooden Horse Gate before riding.

sentences.zh: 管崇嗣為王都虞候，先王上馬，真卿進狀彈之。

translations.literal: Guan Chongsi was the prince's chief inspector and mounted before the prince; Zhenqing submitted a memorial impeaching him.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Chongsi, the prince's chief inspector, mounted before the prince did; Zhenqing memorialized to impeach him.

sentences.zh: 肅宗曰：「朕兒子每出，諄諄教誡之，故不敢失禮。

translations.literal: Suzong said: 'Whenever Our son goes out We earnestly instruct and admonish him, so he dares not lose propriety.'
translations.idiomatic: Suzong said, "I instruct my son earnestly whenever he goes forth, so he would not breach etiquette."

sentences.zh: 崇嗣老將，有足疾，姑欲優容之，卿勿復言。

translations.literal: Chongsi is an old general with a foot ailment; for the moment We wish to treat him leniently—do not speak further.'
translations.idiomatic: Chongsi is an old general with a foot ailment; for now I wish to be lenient—say no more."

sentences.zh: 」乃以奏狀還真卿。

translations.literal: ' He thereupon returned the memorial to Zhenqing.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor returned the memorial to Zhenqing.

sentences.zh: 雖天子蒙塵，典法不廢。

translations.literal: Although the Son of Heaven suffered in the dust, the canonical rites and laws were not abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Even though the emperor had fallen on hard times in exile, he did not neglect ritual and law.

sentences.zh: 洎鑾輿將復宮闕，遣左司郎中李巽先行，陳告宗廟之禮，有司署祝文，稱「嗣皇帝」。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage was about to return to the palace halls, he dispatched Li Xun, Director of the Left Department of the Secretariat, to go ahead and announce the rites at the ancestral temple; the relevant officials drafted the prayer text, calling him "the succeeding emperor."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor's carriage was about to return to the capital, Li Xun of the Secretariat was sent ahead to announce the temple rites. The officials drafted the prayer text, referring to the emperor as "the succeeding Son of Heaven."

sentences.zh: 真卿謂禮儀使崔器曰：「上皇在蜀，可乎？

translations.literal: Zhenqing said to the Commissioner of Ritual, Cui Qi: "The Retired Emperor is in Shu—is this acceptable?"
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhenqing said to Cui Qi, the commissioner of ritual: "The Retired Emperor is still in Shu—is this acceptable?"

sentences.zh: 」器遽奏改之。

translations.literal: Qi immediately memorialized to have it changed.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Qi immediately memorialized the throne to have the wording changed.

sentences.zh: 中旨宣勞，以為名儒深達禮體。

translations.literal: An imperial decree commended him, holding that as a renowned scholar he deeply understood the substance of ritual.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial message praised him, acknowledging that as a leading scholar he had a deep grasp of ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 時太廟為賊所毀，真卿奏曰：「春秋時，新宮災，魯成公三日哭。

translations.literal: At that time the Imperial Ancestral Temple had been destroyed by rebels. Zhenqing memorialized, saying: "In the Spring and Autumn period, when the new palace caught fire, Duke Cheng of Lu wept for three days."
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Imperial Ancestral Temple had been destroyed by rebels. Yan Zhenqing memorialized: "In the Spring and Autumn period, when the new palace burned, Duke Cheng of Lu mourned for three days."

sentences.zh: 今太廟既為盜毀，請築壇於野，皇帝東向哭，然後遣使。

translations.literal: Now that the Imperial Ancestral Temple has been destroyed by bandits, I ask that an altar be built in the open countryside, that the emperor face east and weep, and then that emissaries be dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Imperial Ancestral Temple has been destroyed by rebels, I ask that an altar be built in the open country, that the emperor face east and mourn, and only then send out envoys.

sentences.zh: 」竟不能從。

translations.literal: In the end they could not follow his advice.
translations.idiomatic: In the end his proposal was not adopted.

sentences.zh: 軍國之事，知無不言。

translations.literal: On matters of state and military affairs, he spoke whenever he knew something.
translations.idiomatic: On military and state affairs, he spoke out whenever he had something to say.

sentences.zh: 為宰相所忌，出為同州刺史，轉蒲州刺史。

translations.literal: Envied by the chief ministers, he was sent out as prefect of Tong Prefecture, then transferred to be prefect of Pu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Resented by the chief ministers, he was sent out to serve as prefect of Tong Prefecture, then transferred to Pu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 為御史唐旻所構，貶饒州刺史。

translations.literal: Framed by the censor Tang Min, he was demoted to prefect of Rao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Framed by the censor Tang Min, he was demoted to prefect of Rao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 旋拜升州刺史、浙江西道節度使，征為刑部尚書。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was appointed prefect of Sheng Prefecture and military commissioner of the Zhejiang West Circuit, then summoned to serve as Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed prefect of Sheng Prefecture and military commissioner of the Zhejiang West Circuit, then recalled to serve as Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 李輔國矯詔遷玄宗居西宮，真卿乃首率百僚上表請問起居，輔國惡之，奏貶蓬州長史。

translations.literal: Li Fuguo forged an edict to move Emperor Xuanzong to the Western Palace. Zhenqing was the first to lead the hundred officials in submitting a memorial inquiring after the emperor's health. Fuguo hated this and memorialized to have him demoted to senior administrator of Peng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fuguo forged an edict moving Emperor Xuanzong to the Western Palace. Yan Zhenqing was the first to lead the whole court in submitting a memorial inquiring after the retired emperor's health. Fuguo resented this and had him demoted to senior administrator of Peng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 代宗嗣位，拜利州刺史，遷戶部侍郎，除荊南節度使，未行而罷，除尚書左丞。

translations.literal: When Emperor Daizong succeeded to the throne, he was appointed prefect of Li Prefecture, promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue, appointed military commissioner of Jingnan, dismissed before taking up the post, and appointed Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Daizong came to the throne, Yan Zhenqing was appointed prefect of Li Prefecture, then promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue and named military commissioner of Jingnan. Before he could take up that post he was removed from it and appointed Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 車駕自陜將還，真卿請皇帝先謁五陵、九廟而後還宮。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage was about to return from Shaan, Zhenqing asked that the emperor first visit the Five Tombs and the Nine Temples before returning to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: As the imperial carriage was about to return from Shaan, Yan Zhenqing asked that the emperor visit the Five Tombs and the Nine Temples before returning to the palace.

sentences.zh: 宰相元載謂真卿曰：「公所見雖美，其如不合事宜何？

translations.literal: Chief Minister Yuan Zai said to Zhenqing: "Your view, though fine, what of its failure to fit present circumstances?"
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Yuan Zai said to Yan Zhenqing: "Your view is admirable, but what of the fact that it does not suit present circumstances?"

sentences.zh: 」真卿怒，前曰：「用舍在相公耳，言者何罪？

translations.literal: Zhenqing, angry, stepped forward and said: "Whether I am employed or dismissed rests with the chief minister—but what crime is there in speaking?"
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhenqing stepped forward angrily and said: "Whether I am kept or dismissed is for you to decide—but what crime is there in speaking out?"

sentences.zh: 然朝廷之事，豈堪相公再破除耶！

translations.literal: Yet how can the affairs of the court again be dismantled by the chief minister!
translations.idiomatic: Yet how can the chief minister again tear down the institutions of the court!

sentences.zh: 」載深銜之。

translations.literal: Zai deeply harbored resentment against him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zai deeply resented him.

sentences.zh: 旋改檢校刑部尚書知省事，累進封魯郡公。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was changed to Acting Minister of Justice with charge of routine affairs, and through successive promotions was enfeoffed as Duke of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Acting Minister of Justice with charge of routine affairs, and in time was enfeoffed as Duke of Lu.

sentences.zh: 時元載引用私黨，懼朝臣論奏其短，乃請：百官凡欲論事，皆先白長官，長官白宰相，然後上聞。

translations.literal: At that time Yuan Zai was appointing his own partisans. Fearing that court officials would discuss and memorialize his faults, he requested: whenever officials of any rank wished to discuss affairs, they must first inform their department head; the department head would inform the chief minister, and only then would the matter reach the throne.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yuan Zai was filling the government with his own men. Fearing that court officials would report his misconduct, he proposed that whenever any official wished to raise a matter, he must first inform his department head, who would inform the chief minister, and only then would the matter reach the emperor.

sentences.zh: 真卿上疏曰：

translations.literal: Zhenqing submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhenqing submitted a memorial, saying:

sentences.zh: 御史中丞李進等傳宰相語，稱奉進止：「緣諸司官奏事頗多，朕不憚省覽，但所奏多挾讒毀；

translations.literal: The Assistant Censor-in-Chief Li Jin and others conveyed the chief minister's words, stating that they followed his instructions: "Because officials of the various departments submit memorials in great number, I do not shrink from reviewing them, but many of the submissions are laced with slander;"
