translations.idiomatic: The Assistant Censor-in-Chief Li Jin and others conveyed the chief minister's words, stating that they followed his instructions: "Because officials of the various departments submit memorials in great number, I do not shrink from reviewing them, but many of the submissions are laced with slander;"

sentences.zh: 自今論事者，諸司官皆須先白長官，長官白宰相，宰相定可否，然後奏聞者。

translations.literal: from now on, those who wish to discuss affairs must first inform their department heads; the department heads must inform the chief minister; the chief minister decides whether the matter is acceptable, and only then is it memorialized to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: from now on, those who wish to discuss affairs must first inform their department heads; the department heads must inform the chief minister; the chief minister decides whether the matter is acceptable, and only then is it memorialized to the throne.

sentences.zh: 」臣自聞此語已來，朝野囂然，人心亦多衰退。

translations.literal: Since I heard these words, court and countryside have been in an uproar, and many people's spirits have also fallen away.
translations.idiomatic: Since I heard this policy announced, court and countryside have been in uproar, and many hearts have grown timid.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why is this?
translations.idiomatic: Why is this?

sentences.zh: 諸司長官皆達官也，言皆專達於天子也。

translations.literal: The heads of the various departments are all high officials, and their words all reach the Son of Heaven directly and exclusively.
translations.idiomatic: The heads of the various departments are high officials whose words reach the emperor directly on their own authority.

sentences.zh: 郎官、御史者，陛下腹心耳目之臣也。

translations.literal: Gentlemen of the departments and censors are Your Majesty's trusted eyes and ears.
translations.idiomatic: Gentlemen of the departments and the censors are Your Majesty's own eyes and ears.

sentences.zh: 故其出使天下，事無巨細得失，皆令訪察，回日奏聞，所以明四目、達四聰也。

translations.literal: Therefore when they are sent out across the realm, no matter how great or small the gain or loss, they are all ordered to investigate; on their return they memorialize what they find—this is how the four eyes are made clear and the four ears made keen.
translations.idiomatic: That is why, when they are sent out across the empire, they are charged to investigate everything, great or small, and report back on their return—this is how the ruler keeps wide-open eyes and ears.

sentences.zh: 今陛下欲自屏耳目，使不聰明，則天下何述焉。

translations.literal: Now if Your Majesty wishes to block your own eyes and ears and make yourself unable to hear or see clearly, then what will the realm have to report?
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty now shuts off your own eyes and ears and refuses to see or hear clearly, what will the realm have left to tell you?

sentences.zh: 《詩》云：「營營青蠅，止於棘。

translations.literal: The Book of Odes says: "Buzzing blue flies stop on the thorns."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Odes says: "Buzzing blue flies settle on the thorns."

sentences.zh: 讒言罔極，交亂四國。

translations.literal: Slanderous words know no limit and together throw the four states into chaos.
translations.idiomatic: Slander knows no bounds and together throws the four states into chaos.

sentences.zh: 」以其能變白為黑，變黑為白也。

translations.literal: This is because slander can turn white into black and black into white.
translations.idiomatic: This is because slander can turn white into black and black into white.

sentences.zh: 詩人深惡之，故曰：「取彼讒人，投畀豺虎。

translations.literal: The poet deeply hated this, and therefore said: "Take those slanderers and cast them to the wolves and tigers."
translations.idiomatic: The poet hated this deeply, and so said: "Take those slanderers and throw them to the wolves and tigers."

sentences.zh: 豺虎不食，投畀有北。

translations.literal: If the wolves and tigers will not eat them, cast them to the northern wastes.
translations.idiomatic: If the wolves and tigers will not eat them, throw them to the northern wastes.

sentences.zh: 」則夏之伯明、楚之無極、漢之江充，皆讒人也，孰不惡之？

translations.literal: Then Bo Ming of Xia, Wuji of Chu, and Jiang Chong of Han were all slanderers—who did not hate them?
translations.idiomatic: Bo Ming of Xia, Wuji of Chu, and Jiang Chong of Han were all slanderers—who did not hate such men?

sentences.zh: 陛下惡之，深得君人之體矣。

translations.literal: Your Majesty hates this—you have deeply grasped the way of a ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's hatred of slander shows that you truly understand what it means to be a ruler.

sentences.zh: 陛下何不深回聽察，其言虛誣者，則讒人也，因誅殛之；

translations.literal: Why does Your Majesty not deeply reconsider and listen and investigate? Those whose words are false and calumnious are slanderers—execute them accordingly;
translations.idiomatic: Why does Your Majesty not examine matters more carefully? Those whose accusations prove false are slanderers, and should be punished;

sentences.zh: 其言不虛者，則正人也，因獎勵之。

translations.literal: those whose words are not false are upright men—reward them accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: those whose accusations prove true are upright men, and should be rewarded.

sentences.zh: 陛下舍此不為，使眾人皆謂陛下不能明察，倦於聽覽，以此為辭，拒其諫諍，臣竊為陛下痛惜之。

translations.literal: Your Majesty forsakes this and does not do it, so that everyone says Your Majesty cannot see clearly, is weary of listening, and uses this as a pretext to reject remonstrance. I privately grieve for Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has chosen not to do this, so that everyone will say you cannot see clearly, that you are weary of listening, and that you are using this policy as an excuse to reject honest counsel. I cannot but grieve for Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 臣聞太宗勤於聽覽，庶政以理，故著《司門式》云：「其有無門籍人，有急奏者，皆令監門司與仗家引奏，不許關礙。

translations.literal: I have heard that Emperor Taizong was diligent in listening and reviewing, and common affairs were thereby put in order. Therefore he set down in the Gate Office Regulations: "If someone without a gate pass has an urgent memorial, the Gate Guard Office and the palace guard are both to lead him in to memorialize, and no obstruction is permitted."
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that Emperor Taizong was diligent in listening and reviewing, and common affairs were thereby put in order. Therefore he set down in the Gate Office Regulations: "If someone without a gate pass has an urgent memorial, the Gate Guard Office and the palace guard are both to lead him in to memorialize, and no obstruction is permitted."

sentences.zh: 」所以防壅蔽也。

translations.literal: This was to guard against blockage and concealment.
translations.idiomatic: This was meant to guard against obstruction and concealment.

sentences.zh: 並置立仗馬二匹，須有乘騎便往，所以平治天下，正用此道也。

translations.literal: He also kept two standing guard horses ready, so that whenever there was urgent business one could mount and go at once—this was precisely the way by which he brought peace and order to the realm.
translations.idiomatic: He also kept two horses saddled and ready in the palace guard, so that urgent business could be carried to him at once. This was precisely how he kept the realm in order.

sentences.zh: 天寶已後，李林甫威權日盛，群臣不先諮宰相輒奏事者，仍托以他故中傷，猶不敢明約百司，令先白宰相。

translations.literal: After the Tianbao era, as Li Linfu's power and authority grew daily, any minister who memorialized without first consulting the chief minister would still be wounded on some other pretext, yet he still did not dare openly require all offices to inform the chief minister first.
translations.idiomatic: After the Tianbao era, as Li Linfu's power and authority grew daily, any minister who memorialized without first consulting the chief minister would still be attacked on some other pretext, yet even he did not dare openly require all offices to inform the chief minister first.

sentences.zh: 又閹官袁思藝日宣詔至中書，玄宗動靜，必告林甫，先意奏請，玄宗驚喜若神。

translations.literal: Moreover, the eunuch Yuan Siyi daily carried edicts to the Secretariat; whatever Emperor Xuanzong did or did not do, he always told Linfu in advance, who would memorialize requests before they were needed. Xuanzong was astonished and delighted as though at the work of a god.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the eunuch Yuan Siyi daily carried edicts to the Secretariat; whatever Emperor Xuanzong did or did not do, he always told Linfu in advance, who would memorialize requests before they were needed. Xuanzong was astonished and delighted as though at the work of a god.

sentences.zh: 以此權柄恩寵日甚，道路以目。

translations.literal: By this means his power and favor grew daily; people did not even dare meet one another's eyes in the streets.
translations.idiomatic: By this means his power and imperial favor grew daily, until people were afraid even to meet one another's eyes in the streets.

sentences.zh: 上意不下宣，下情不上達，所以漸致潼關之禍，皆權臣誤主，不遵太宗之法故也。

translations.literal: The sovereign's intent was not carried down, and the feelings of those below did not reach above—therefore the disaster at Tong Pass gradually arose. All of this was because powerful ministers misled their ruler and did not follow Emperor Taizong's methods.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign's intent was not carried down, and the feelings of those below did not reach above—therefore the disaster at Tong Pass gradually arose. All of this was because powerful ministers misled their ruler and did not follow Emperor Taizong's methods.

sentences.zh: 陵夷至於今日，天下之蔽，盡萃於聖躬，豈陛下招致之乎？

translations.literal: Decline has carried us down to today; all the concealment in the realm has gathered upon Your Sacred Person—did Your Majesty bring this upon yourself?
translations.idiomatic: Decline has carried us down to today; all the concealment in the realm has gathered upon Your Sacred Person—did Your Majesty bring this upon yourself?

sentences.zh: 蓋其所從來者漸矣。

translations.literal: It was rather that what led to this came little by little over time.
translations.idiomatic: Rather, it arose gradually over time.

sentences.zh: 自艱難之初，百姓尚未彫弊，太平之理，立可便致。

translations.literal: From the very beginning of the crisis, the common people had not yet been worn down; the principles of peace could immediately have been restored.
translations.idiomatic: At the very start of the crisis, the people had not yet been worn down, and peace could still have been restored at once.

sentences.zh: 屬李輔國用權，宰相專政，遞相姑息，莫肯直言。

translations.literal: But Li Fuguo wielded power, the chief ministers monopolized government, and they indulged one another in turn, none willing to speak frankly.
translations.idiomatic: But Li Fuguo wielded power, the chief ministers monopolized government, and they indulged one another in turn, none willing to speak frankly.

sentences.zh: 大開三司，不安反側，逆賊散落，將士北走党項，合集士賊，至今為患。

translations.literal: They broadly opened the Three Commissions, could not set the restless at ease, rebels scattered, soldiers fled north to the Tangut tribes, gathered bandits together, and this remains a plague to this day.
translations.idiomatic: They broadly opened the Three Commissions, could not set the restless at ease, rebels scattered, soldiers fled north to the Tangut tribes, gathered bandits together, and this remains a plague to this day.

sentences.zh: 偽將更相驚恐，因思明危懼，扇動卻反。

translations.literal: Rebel generals frightened one another in turn; because Shi Siming was fearful, he was stirred up and turned against the court again.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel generals frightened one another in turn; because Shi Siming was fearful, he was stirred up and turned against the court again.

sentences.zh: 又今相州敗散，東都陷沒，先帝由此憂勤，至於損壽，臣每思之，痛切心骨。

translations.literal: Moreover, now that the defeat and dispersal at Xiang Prefecture and the fall of the Eastern Capital had worn down the Late Emperor until his life was shortened, each time I think of this my heart and bones ache.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the defeat at Xiang Prefecture and the fall of the Eastern Capital wore the Late Emperor down until his life was shortened. Each time I think of it, grief cuts me to the bone.

sentences.zh: 今天下兵戈未戢，瘡痏未平，陛下豈得不日聞讜言以廣視聽，而欲頓隔忠讜之路乎！

translations.literal: Now warfare under Heaven has not yet been stilled, wounds not yet healed—how can Your Majesty fail to daily hear frank speech to broaden your sight and hearing, yet wish suddenly to block the path of loyal remonstrance!
translations.idiomatic: Now warfare under Heaven has not yet been stilled, wounds not yet healed—how can Your Majesty fail to daily hear frank speech to broaden your sight and hearing, yet wish suddenly to block the path of loyal remonstrance!

sentences.zh: 臣竊聞陛下在陜州時，奏事者不限貴賤，務廣聞見，乃堯、舜之事也。

translations.literal: I have privately heard that when Your Majesty was at Shaan Prefecture, those who memorialized were not limited by rank high or low, and every effort was made to broaden what was heard and seen—this was the conduct of Yao and Shun.
translations.idiomatic: I have privately heard that when Your Majesty was at Shaan Prefecture, those who memorialized were not limited by rank high or low, and every effort was made to broaden what was heard and seen—this was the conduct of Yao and Shun.

sentences.zh: 凡百臣庶以為太宗之理，可翹足而待也。

translations.literal: All officials and commoners thought that the order of Emperor Taizong could be awaited with feet tucked up in ease.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and commoners alike thought that a reign like Emperor Taizong's could be expected at any moment.

sentences.zh: 臣又聞君子難進易退，由此言之，朝廷開不諱之路，猶恐不言，況懷厭怠，令宰相宣進止，使御史臺作條目，不令直進。

translations.literal: I have also heard that for a gentleman it is hard to advance and easy to withdraw. From this it follows that even when the court opens a path where nothing is taboo, there is still fear that men will not speak—how much more so when there is weariness and slackness, when the chief minister announces decisions in advance, and when the Censorate is made to draw up regulations forbidding direct access!
translations.idiomatic: I have also heard that for a gentleman it is hard to advance and easy to withdraw. From this it follows that even when the court opens a path where nothing is taboo, there is still fear that men will not speak—how much more so when there is weariness and slackness, when the chief minister announces decisions in advance, and when the Censorate is made to draw up regulations forbidding direct access!

sentences.zh: 從此人人不敢奏事，則陛下聞見，只在三數人耳。

translations.literal: From this point on, if no one dares to memorialize, then what Your Majesty hears and sees will come from only two or three people.
translations.idiomatic: From this point on, if no one dares to memorialize, then what Your Majesty hears and sees will come from only two or three people.

sentences.zh: 天下之士，方鉗口結舌，陛下後見無人奏事，必謂朝廷無事可論，豈知懼不敢進，即林甫、國忠復起矣。

translations.literal: Men of talent under Heaven are just now clamping shut their mouths. Later, when Your Majesty sees that no one memorializes, you will surely think the court has no affairs worth discussing—how would you know they are afraid and dare not come forward? In that case Li Linfu and Yang Guozhong will rise again.
translations.idiomatic: Men of talent under Heaven are just now clamping shut their mouths. Later, when Your Majesty sees that no one memorializes, you will surely think the court has no affairs worth discussing—how would you know they are afraid and dare not come forward? In that case Li Linfu and Yang Guozhong will rise again.

sentences.zh: 凡百臣庶，以為危殆之期，又翹足而至也。

translations.literal: All officials and commoners will think the hour of peril is again at hand, and will await it with feet tucked up in ease.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and commoners alike will think that disaster is again near at hand—and they will not have long to wait.

sentences.zh: 如今日之事，曠古未有，雖李林甫、楊國忠猶不敢公然如此。

translations.literal: A matter like today's has never existed since antiquity; even Li Linfu and Yang Guozhong did not dare to be so openly brazen.
translations.idiomatic: A matter like today's has never existed since antiquity; even Li Linfu and Yang Guozhong did not dare to be so openly brazen.

sentences.zh: 今陛下不早覺悟，漸成孤立，後縱悔之無及矣！

translations.literal: If Your Majesty does not awaken early, you will gradually become isolated, and later even if you regret it there will be no remedy!
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty does not awaken early, you will gradually become isolated, and later even if you regret it there will be no remedy!

sentences.zh: 臣實知忤大臣者，罪在不測，不忍孤負陛下，無任懇迫之至。

translations.literal: I truly know that one who offends a chief minister faces punishment beyond measure, yet I cannot bear to fail Your Majesty—my earnest urgency knows no bound.
translations.idiomatic: I know full well that to offend a chief minister is to risk punishment beyond measure, yet I cannot bear to fail Your Majesty. I plead with all the urgency I can muster.

sentences.zh: 其激切如此。

translations.literal: His remonstrance was this impassioned.
translations.idiomatic: His remonstrance was this fierce and impassioned.

sentences.zh: 於是中人爭寫內本布於外。

translations.literal: Thereupon eunuchs competed to copy the inner text and spread it outside.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs then competed to copy the memorial and circulate it outside the palace.

sentences.zh: 後攝祭太廟，以祭器不修言於朝，載坐以誹謗，貶硤州別駕、撫州湖州刺史。

translations.literal: Later, while acting as officiant at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, he spoke in court about the sacrificial vessels not being properly maintained. Zai convicted him of slander and had him demoted to vice-prefect of Xia Prefecture, then prefect of Fu and Hu Prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Later, while acting as officiant at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, he spoke in court about the sacrificial vessels not being properly maintained. Yuan Zai convicted him of slander and had him demoted to vice-prefect of Xia Prefecture, then prefect of Fu and Hu Prefectures.

sentences.zh: 元載伏誅，拜刑部尚書。

translations.literal: When Yuan Zai was executed, he was appointed Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuan Zai was executed, Yan Zhenqing was appointed Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 代宗崩，為禮儀使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Daizong died, he served as Commissioner of Ritual.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Daizong died, he was made commissioner of ritual.

sentences.zh: 又以高祖已下七聖謚號繁多，乃上議請取初謚為定。

translations.literal: Also, because the posthumous titles of the seven sages from Emperor Gaozu downward had become numerous, he submitted a proposal asking that the original posthumous titles be taken as fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Also, because the posthumous titles of the seven sage emperors from Emperor Gaozu downward had become numerous, he submitted a proposal asking that the original posthumous titles be taken as fixed.

sentences.zh: 袁傪以諂言排之，遂罷。

translations.literal: Yuan Cuan blocked him with flattery and opposition, and the proposal was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Cuan blocked him with flattery and opposition, and the proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 楊炎為相，惡之，改太子少傅，禮儀使如舊，外示崇寵，實去其權也。

translations.literal: When Yang Yan became chief minister, he hated him and changed his post to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent while leaving him Commissioner of Ritual as before—outwardly showing honor, but in fact removing his authority.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Yan became chief minister, he hated him and changed his post to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent while leaving him commissioner of ritual as before—outwardly showing honor, but in fact removing his authority.

sentences.zh: 盧杞專權，忌之，改太子太師，罷禮儀使，諭於真卿曰：「方面之任，何處為便？

translations.literal: When Lu Qi monopolized power, he envied him, changed his post to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, removed him as Commissioner of Ritual, and said to Zhenqing: "For a regional appointment, which place would suit you best?"
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Qi monopolized power, he envied him, changed his post to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, removed him as commissioner of ritual, and said to Yan Zhenqing: "For a regional appointment, which place would suit you best?"

sentences.zh: 」真卿候杞於中書曰：「真卿以褊性為小人所憎，竄逐非一。

translations.literal: Zhenqing waited for Qi at the Secretariat and said: "Zhenqing, because of my narrow temperament, has been hated by petty men and banished more than once."
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhenqing waited for Lu Qi at the Secretariat and said: "Because of my narrow temperament, I have been hated by petty men and banished more than once."

sentences.zh: 今已羸老，幸相公庇之。

translations.literal: Now I am worn and old; I am fortunate if the chief minister will shelter me.
translations.idiomatic: Now I am worn and old; I am fortunate if the chief minister will shelter me.

sentences.zh: 相公先中丞傳首至平原，面上血真卿不敢衣拭，以舌舐之，相公忍不相容乎？

translations.literal: When the chief minister's late brother, the assistant censor-in-chief, sent his head to Pingyuan, I did not dare wipe the blood from his face with my clothes, but licked it with my tongue—can the chief minister bear not to tolerate me?
translations.idiomatic: When your late brother, the assistant censor-in-chief, sent his head to Pingyuan, I did not dare wipe the blood from his face with my clothes, but licked it with my tongue—can you bear not to tolerate me?

sentences.zh: 」杞矍然下拜，而含怒心。

translations.literal: Qi started back and bowed, but harbored anger in his heart.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qi started back and bowed, but nursed rage in his heart.

sentences.zh: 會李希烈陷汝州，杞乃奏曰：「顏真卿四方所信，使諭之，可不勞師旅。

translations.literal: When Li Xilie captured Ru Prefecture, Qi memorialized, saying: "Yan Zhenqing is trusted throughout the four directions; if he is sent to persuade Xilie, troops need not be mobilized."
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xilie captured Ru Prefecture, Lu Qi memorialized, saying: "Yan Zhenqing is trusted throughout the empire; if he is sent to persuade Xilie, troops need not be mobilized."

sentences.zh: 」上從之，朝廷失色，李勉聞之，以為失一元老，貽朝廷羞，乃密表請留。

translations.literal: The emperor agreed. The court turned pale. When Li Mian heard of it, he thought the court would lose a senior elder and bring shame on the dynasty, and secretly memorialized asking that Zhenqing be kept.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed. The court turned pale. When Li Mian heard of it, he thought the court would lose a senior elder and bring shame on the dynasty, and secretly memorialized asking that Yan Zhenqing be kept.

sentences.zh: 又遣逆於路，不及。

translations.literal: He also sent men to intercept him on the road, but they did not arrive in time.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent men to intercept him on the road, but they did not arrive in time.

sentences.zh: 初見希烈，欲宣詔旨，希烈養子千余人露刃爭前迫真卿，將食其肉。

translations.literal: When he first met Xilie and was about to announce the edict, Xilie's adopted sons, more than a thousand men, bared their blades and pressed forward together on Zhenqing, about to eat his flesh.
translations.idiomatic: When he first met Li Xilie and was about to announce the imperial edict, more than a thousand of Xilie's adopted sons drew their blades and pressed in on Yan Zhenqing, threatening to cut him to pieces.

sentences.zh: 諸將叢繞慢罵，舉刃以擬之，真卿不動。

translations.literal: The generals clustered around cursing and insulting him, raising blades and pointing them at him; Zhenqing did not move.
translations.idiomatic: The generals swarmed around cursing and insulting him, raising their blades at him, but Yan Zhenqing did not stir.

sentences.zh: 希烈遽以身蔽之，而麾其眾，眾退，乃揖真卿就館舍。

translations.literal: Xilie hastily shielded him with his own body, waved off his followers, and when they withdrew, bowed to Zhenqing and led him to the guest lodge.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xilie quickly shielded him with his own body, waved off his men, and when they withdrew, bowed to Yan Zhenqing and escorted him to quarters.

sentences.zh: 因逼為章表，令雪己，願罷兵馬。

translations.literal: Thereupon he pressed him to draft a memorial clearing his name and asking that troops be withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he pressed him to draft a memorial clearing his name and asking that troops be withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 累遣真卿兄子峴與從吏凡數輩繼來京師。

translations.literal: Repeatedly he sent Zhenqing's nephew Xian and several parties of attendant officials in succession to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Repeatedly he sent Yan Zhenqing's nephew Xian and several parties of attendant officials in succession to the capital.

sentences.zh: 上皆不報。

translations.literal: The emperor responded to none of them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gave no response to any of them.

sentences.zh: 每於諸子書，令嚴奉家廟，恤諸孤而已。

translations.literal: In each letter to his sons he wrote only to keep the family temple strictly maintained and care for the orphans.
translations.idiomatic: In each letter to his sons he wrote only to maintain the family temple faithfully and care for the orphans.

sentences.zh: 希烈大宴逆黨，召真卿坐，使觀倡優斥黷朝政為戲，真卿怒曰：「相公，人臣也，奈何使此曹如是乎？

translations.literal: Xilie gave a great banquet for the rebel party, summoned Zhenqing to sit, and had him watch singers and actors revile and profane the court in mockery. Zhenqing said angrily: "Sir, you are a subject of the throne—how can you let these people behave like this?"
translations.idiomatic: Li Xilie gave a great banquet for the rebel party, summoned Yan Zhenqing to sit, and had him watch singers and actors revile and profane the court in mockery. Yan Zhenqing said angrily: "Sir, you are a subject of the throne—how can you let these people behave like this?"

sentences.zh: 」拂衣而起，希烈慚，亦呵止。

translations.literal: He brushed his robes and rose. Xilie was ashamed and also shouted for it to stop.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhenqing brushed off his robes and stood up. Li Xilie was ashamed and shouted for the performance to stop.

sentences.zh: 時朱滔、王武俊、田悅、李納使在坐，目真卿謂希烈曰：「聞太師名德久矣，相公欲建大號，而太師至，非天命正位？

translations.literal: At that time the envoys of Zhu Tao, Wang Wujun, Tian Yue, and Li Na were seated there. They looked at Zhenqing and said to Xilie: "We have long heard of the Grand Preceptor's fame and virtue. Sir, you wish to assume a great title—and now the Grand Preceptor has arrived. Is this not Heaven's mandate for a rightful enthronement?"
translations.idiomatic: At that time the envoys of Zhu Tao, Wang Wujun, Tian Yue, and Li Na were seated there. They looked at Yan Zhenqing and said to Li Xilie: "We have long heard of the Grand Preceptor's fame and virtue. Sir, you wish to assume a great title—and now the Grand Preceptor has arrived. Is this not Heaven's mandate for a rightful enthronement?"

sentences.zh: 欲求宰相，孰先太師乎？

translations.literal: If you seek a chief minister, who should come before the Grand Preceptor?
translations.idiomatic: If you seek a chief minister, who should come before the Grand Preceptor?

sentences.zh: 」真卿正色叱之曰：「是何宰相耶！

translations.literal: Zhenqing sternly rebuked them, saying: "What sort of chief minister would that be!"
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhenqing sternly rebuked them, saying: "What sort of chief minister would that be!"

sentences.zh: 君等聞顏杲卿無？

translations.literal: Have you gentlemen not heard of Yan Gaoqing?
translations.idiomatic: Have you gentlemen not heard of Yan Gaoqing?

sentences.zh: 是吾兄也。

translations.literal: He was my elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: He was my elder brother.

sentences.zh: 祿山反，首舉義兵，及被害，詬罵不絕於口。

translations.literal: When Lushan rebelled, he was the first to raise the loyal army, and when he was killed he did not stop cursing to the end.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rebelled, he was the first to raise loyal troops, and when he was killed he cursed his captors without ceasing.

sentences.zh: 吾今生向八十，官至太師，守吾兄之節，死而後已，豈受汝輩誘脅耶！

translations.literal: I am now nearly eighty years old, have reached the rank of Grand Preceptor, and will uphold my brother's integrity until death—would I accept your kind's seduction and coercion!
translations.idiomatic: I am nearly eighty, have risen to Grand Preceptor, and will uphold my brother's integrity until I die. Do you think I would yield to your threats and blandishments!

sentences.zh: 」諸賊不敢復出口。

translations.literal: The rebels dared not speak again.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels dared not speak again.

sentences.zh: 希烈乃拘真卿，令甲士十人守，掘方丈坎於庭，曰「坑顏」，真卿怡然不介意。

translations.literal: Xilie then detained Zhenqing, set ten armored soldiers to guard him, dug a square zhang pit in the courtyard labeled "the pit for Yan," yet Zhenqing was calmly unconcerned.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xilie then detained Yan Zhenqing, set ten armored soldiers to guard him, and dug a square pit in the courtyard labeled "Yan's pit," but Yan Zhenqing remained calm and unconcerned.

sentences.zh: 後張伯儀敗績於安州，希烈令賚伯儀旌節首級誇示真卿，真卿慟哭投地。

translations.literal: Later Zhang Boyi was defeated at An Prefecture. Xilie had Boyi's banner of command and severed head brought to display to Zhenqing in boast. Zhenqing wept in grief and threw himself to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhang Boyi was defeated at An Prefecture. Li Xilie had Boyi's banner of command and severed head brought to display to Yan Zhenqing in boast. Yan Zhenqing wept in grief and threw himself to the ground.

sentences.zh: 後其大將周曾等謀襲汝州，因回兵殺希烈，奉真卿為節度。

translations.literal: Later his generals Zhou Zeng and others plotted to attack Ru Prefecture, turned their troops back and killed Xilie, and installed Zhenqing as military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Later Li Xilie's generals Zhou Zeng and others plotted to strike at Ru Prefecture, turned their troops around and killed Xilie, and proclaimed Yan Zhenqing military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 事泄，希烈殺曾等，遂送真卿於龍興寺。

translations.literal: The affair leaked out; Xilie killed Zeng and the others and thereupon sent Zhenqing to Longxing Temple.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot was exposed, Xilie killed Zeng and his accomplices and sent Zhenqing to Longxing Temple.

sentences.zh: 真卿度必死，乃作遺表，自為墓誌、祭文，常指寢室西壁下云：「吾殯所也。

translations.literal: Zhenqing judged that he would surely die, wrote a final memorial, composed his own epitaph and sacrificial text, and often pointed beneath the west wall of his sleeping chamber, saying: 'This is where I shall be buried.'
translations.idiomatic: Expecting death, Zhenqing drafted a final memorial, wrote his own epitaph and funeral ode, and often pointed to the west wall of his room, saying, "This is where I shall lie."

sentences.zh: 」希烈既陷汴州，僭偽號，使人問儀於真卿，真卿曰：「老夫耄矣，曾掌國禮，所記者諸侯朝覲禮耳。

translations.literal: ' After Xilie had taken Bian prefecture and usurped a false title, he sent men to ask Zhenqing about ritual; Zhenqing said: 'This old man is aged; he once managed state rites—what he remembers is only the ritual of feudal lords paying court.'
translations.idiomatic: " After Xilie seized Bianzhou and declared himself emperor, he asked Zhenqing about court ritual. Zhenqing replied, "I am an old man who once managed state ceremonies—I remember only how feudal lords paid homage to the Son of Heaven."

sentences.zh: 興元元年，王師復振，逆賊慮變起蔡州，乃遣其將辛景臻、安華至真卿所，積柴庭中，沃之以油，且傳逆詞曰：「不能屈節，當自燒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xingyuan the imperial army revived its strength; the rebel bandits feared mutiny would arise at Cai prefecture and sent their generals Xin Jingzhen and An Hua to Zhenqing's place, heaped firewood in the courtyard, poured oil over it, and also transmitted rebel words: 'If you cannot bend your integrity, you should burn yourself.'
translations.idiomatic: In Xingyuan year 1, as imperial forces rallied, the rebels feared a coup at Caizhou and sent generals Xin Jingzhen and An Hua to Zhenqing's quarters. They piled firewood in the courtyard, drenched it with oil, and announced: "If you will not submit, burn yourself."

sentences.zh: 」真卿乃投身赴火，景臻等遽止之，復告希烈。

translations.literal: ' Zhenqing thereupon threw himself toward the fire; Jingzhen and the others hastily stopped him and again reported to Xilie.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhenqing threw himself toward the flames; Jingzhen and the others pulled him back and reported to Xilie.

sentences.zh: 德宗復宮闕，希烈弟希倩在朱泚黨中，例伏誅。

translations.literal: Dezong recovered the palace; Xilie's younger brother Xiqian was among Zhu Ci's faction and was executed according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong recovered the capital, Xilie's brother Xiqian, who had joined Zhu Ci's faction, was executed.

sentences.zh: 希烈聞之怒。

translations.literal: Xilie heard of this and was enraged.
translations.idiomatic: Xilie flew into a rage on hearing the news.

sentences.zh: 興元元年八月三日，乃使閹奴與景臻等殺真卿。

translations.literal: On the third day of the eighth month of the first year of Xingyuan he sent eunuch slaves with Jingzhen and others to kill Zhenqing.
translations.idiomatic: On the third day of the eighth month of Xingyuan year 1 he sent eunuchs with Jingzhen and others to kill Zhenqing.

sentences.zh: 先曰：「有敕」。

translations.literal: First they said: 'There is an edict.'
translations.idiomatic: They announced, "There is an edict."

sentences.zh: 真卿拜，奴曰：「宜賜卿死。

translations.literal: Zhenqing bowed; the slave said: 'You should be granted death.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhenqing bowed. The eunuch said, "You are sentenced to death."

sentences.zh: 」真卿曰：「老臣無狀，罪當死，然不知使人何日從長安來？

translations.literal: ' Zhenqing said: 'This old minister is without merit and deserves death, yet I do not know on what day the envoy came from Chang'an?'
translations.idiomatic: " Zhenqing said, "This old servant deserves death—but when did the envoy leave Chang'an?"

sentences.zh: 」奴曰：「從大梁來。

translations.literal: ' The slave said: 'From Daliang.'
translations.idiomatic: " The eunuch replied, "From Daliang."

sentences.zh: 」真卿罵曰：「乃逆賊耳，何敕耶！

translations.literal: ' Zhenqing cursed: 'You are nothing but a rebel bandit—what edict is there!'
translations.idiomatic: " Zhenqing shouted, "You are a traitor—what edict is there!"

sentences.zh: 」遂縊殺之，年七十七。

translations.literal: ' They thereupon strangled and killed him; he was seventy-seven.
translations.idiomatic: " They strangled him. He was seventy-seven.

sentences.zh: 及淮、泗平，貞元元年，陳仙奇使護送真卿喪歸京師。

translations.literal: When Huai and Si were pacified, in the first year of Zhenyuan Chen Xianqi sent men to escort Zhenqing's coffin back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: After the Huai and Si regions were pacified, in Zhenyuan year 1 Chen Xianqi escorted Zhenqing's coffin to the capital.

sentences.zh: 德宗痛悼異常。

translations.literal: Dezong grieved and mourned beyond the ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong mourned him with extraordinary grief.

sentences.zh: 廢朝五日，謚曰文忠。

translations.literal: Court was suspended for five days; his posthumous title was Cultured and Loyal.
translations.idiomatic: Court was suspended for five days and he was given the posthumous title Cultured and Loyal.

sentences.zh: 復下詔曰：「君臣之義，生錄其功，歿厚其禮，況才優匡國，忠至滅身。

translations.literal: Another edict was issued: 'The meaning between ruler and subject is to record merit in life and enrich rites in death—how much more when talent excels at aiding the state and loyalty reaches to giving one's body.'
translations.idiomatic: Another edict proclaimed: "Between ruler and subject, merit is recorded in life and honors multiplied in death—how much more when talent served the state and loyalty cost one's life."

sentences.zh: 朕自興嘆，勞於寤寐。

translations.literal: We ourselves sigh at the thought and are troubled in waking and sleeping.
translations.idiomatic: We sigh at the thought and are troubled waking and sleeping.

sentences.zh: 故光祿大夫、守太子太師、上柱國、魯郡公顏真卿，器質天資，公忠傑出，出入四朝，堅貞一誌。

translations.literal: The late Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Guardian Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, Supreme Pillar of State, and Duke of Lu Yan Zhenqing—his capacity and nature were heaven-given, his public loyalty outstanding; he passed through four reigns with one steadfast will.
translations.idiomatic: The late Guardian Grand Preceptor Yan Zhenqing, Duke of Lu and Supreme Pillar of State—gifted by nature, outstanding in public loyalty, he served four reigns with unwavering resolve.

sentences.zh: 屬賊臣擾亂，委以存諭，拘肋累歲，死而不撓，稽其盛節，實謂猶生。

translations.literal: When rebel subjects disturbed the realm he was entrusted to preserve and instruct; bound and coerced for years, he died without bending—in examining his lofty integrity, it may truly be said he still lives.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels ravaged the realm he was sent to negotiate; held captive for years, he died unbowed. Such integrity is as if he still lived.

sentences.zh: 朕致貽斯禍，慚悼靡及，式崇嘉命，兼延爾嗣。

translations.literal: We brought upon him this calamity, and shame and grief cannot reach to the end; We therefore exalt him with a fine appointment and extend favor to his heirs.
translations.idiomatic: We brought this calamity upon him and cannot express our shame and grief; We therefore honor him with a grand posthumous rank and extend favor to his descendants.

sentences.zh: 可贈司徒，仍賜布帛五百端。

translations.literal: He may be posthumously made Minister of Education and additionally granted five hundred bolts of cloth and silk.
translations.idiomatic: He is posthumously appointed Minister of Education and granted five hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 男頵、碩等喪制終，所司奏超授官秩。

translations.literal: When his sons Yun, Shuo, and others finished mourning, the relevant offices memorialized to grant them offices above their rank.
translations.idiomatic: When his sons Yun and Shuo completed mourning, the relevant offices recommended them for promotion beyond ordinary rank.

sentences.zh: 」貞元六年十一月南郊，赦書節文授真卿一子五品正員官，故頵得錄用。

translations.literal: ' At the southern suburban sacrifice in the eleventh month of the sixth year of Zhenyuan, the amnesty document's festival text granted one of Zhenqing's sons a regular fifth-rank post, and thus Yun was employed.
translations.idiomatic: " At the southern suburban sacrifice in the eleventh month of Zhenyuan year 6, the amnesty granted one of Zhenqing's sons a regular fifth-rank office, and Yun was appointed.

sentences.zh: 文宗詔曰：「朕每覽國史，見忠烈之臣，未嘗不嗟嘆久之，思有以報。

translations.literal: Wenzong's edict said: 'Whenever We read the dynastic histories and see loyal and valiant subjects, We have never failed to sigh long, thinking how to repay them.'
translations.idiomatic: Wenzong's edict read: "Whenever We read the dynastic histories and encounter loyal martyrs, We sigh long and wonder how to repay them."

sentences.zh: 如聞從覽、弘式，實杲卿、真卿之孫。

translations.literal: We have heard that Conglan and Hongshi are in truth the grandsons of Gao Qing and Zhenqing.
translations.idiomatic: We have heard that Conglan and Hongshi are grandsons of Gao Qing and Zhenqing.

sentences.zh: 永惟九原，既不可作，旌其嗣續，諒協典彜。

translations.literal: Forever thinking of the nine plains, which can no longer be made—We honor their continuing line, surely in accord with canonical norms.
translations.idiomatic: The dead cannot be recalled, but honoring their descendants accords with right principle.

sentences.zh: 考績已深於宦途者，命列於中臺；

translations.literal: Those whose performance evaluations are already deep in official careers shall be ordered to ranks in the central administration;
translations.idiomatic: Those with long service records shall be appointed to central offices;

sentences.zh: 官次未齒於縉紳者，俾佐於左輔。

translations.literal: those whose official standing has not yet taken place among the girdled and sashed shall be made assistants in the left capital district.
translations.idiomatic: those not yet established among officials shall serve as assistants in the capital."

sentences.zh: 庶使天下再新義風。

translations.literal: We hope thereby to renew throughout the realm the wind of righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Thus may the moral wind of the realm be renewed.

sentences.zh: 」以真卿曾孫弘式為同州參軍。

translations.literal: ' Zhenqing's great-grandson Hongshi was made army staff officer of Tong prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhenqing's great-grandson Hongshi was appointed army staff officer of Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：每思先軫免冑，子路結纓，雖云其忠，未聞於道。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Whenever I think of Xian Zhen removing his helmet and Zilu tying his cap-cords—though their loyalty is praised, it is not heard of in the Way.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: I think of Xian Zhen baring his head and Zilu tying his cap-strings—loyal acts, yet not the fullness of the Way.

sentences.zh: 如成公孝於家，能於軍，忠於國，是武之英也；

translations.literal: As for Chenggong, filial in the family, capable in the army, loyal to the state—he is a hero of martial virtue;
translations.idiomatic: Chenggong was filial at home, capable in the field, and loyal to the state—a hero of martial virtue;

sentences.zh: 茍無楊炎弄權，若任之為將，遂展其才，豈有朱泚之禍焉！

translations.literal: if not for Yang Yan's manipulation of power, had he been entrusted as general and allowed to display his talent, how could there have been Zhu Ci's calamity!
translations.idiomatic: had Yang Yan not manipulated power and had he been made a general to use his full talent, would Zhu Ci's disaster have occurred!

sentences.zh: 如清臣富於學，守其正，全其節，昌文之傑也；

translations.literal: as for Qingchen, rich in learning, keeping to the upright, preserving his integrity—he is an outstanding figure of flourishing culture;
translations.idiomatic: Qingchen was learned, upright, and preserved his integrity to the end—a paragon of civil culture;

sentences.zh: 茍無盧杞惡直，若任之為相，遂行其道，豈有希烈之叛焉！

translations.literal: if not for Lu Qi's hatred of the upright, had he been entrusted as chief minister and allowed to carry out his Way, how could there have been Li Xilie's rebellion!
translations.idiomatic: had Lu Qi not hated the upright and had he been made chief minister to enact his policies, would Li Xilie have rebelled!

sentences.zh: 夫國得賢則安，失賢則危。

translations.literal: When a state gains the worthy it is secure; when it loses the worthy it is in peril.
translations.idiomatic: A state with worthy men is secure; without them it is in peril.

sentences.zh: 德宗內信奸邪，外斥良善，幾致危亡，宜哉。

translations.literal: Dezong inwardly trusted the treacherous and wicked and outwardly rejected the good and kind, nearly bringing ruin—it is fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong trusted villains within and rejected the good without, nearly destroying the dynasty—as was fitting.

sentences.zh: 噫，「仁以為己任，不亦重乎；

translations.literal: Alas! 'To take benevolence as one's task—is it not weighty?
translations.idiomatic: Alas! "To take benevolence as one's burden—is it not heavy?

sentences.zh: 死而後已，不亦遠乎！

translations.literal: Only at death does it cease—is it not far-reaching!'
translations.idiomatic: Only at death does one rest—is it not a far-reaching aim!"

sentences.zh: 」二君守道歿身，為時垂訓，希代之士也，光文武之道焉。

translations.literal: ' The two lords kept the Way and died in body, leaving instruction for their age—men rare across generations who glorify the Way of Wen and Wu.
translations.idiomatic: " Both men upheld the Way unto death, leaving lessons for their age—rare spirits who glorify the civil and martial traditions.

sentences.zh: 贊贊曰：自古皆死，得正為順。

translations.literal: The commentator says: From antiquity all die; to obtain the upright is to accord with order.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: All men die; to die upright is to die in accord with Heaven's order.

sentences.zh: 二公云亡，萬代垂訓。

translations.literal: The two lords have passed away, yet their instruction extends through ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: Both men are gone, yet their example instructs ten thousand generations.
